#

Peter,
**A single $10 donation.**
That’s what we’re asking from you today, to help reelect Jon Ossoff and take back the Senate majority for Democrats. We’ll explain more in a minute, but if you can make that donation right now, _thank you._ Here’s the link to chip in: **[https://act.electjon.com/go/Donate](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-jan26.wPRyEn&refcode=em260119-1-full-b&t=1&akid=1470%2E5691347%2EXV17Sg)**
Ok, here’s the deal:

Peter, For more than two decades, American Veterans Center has been dedicated to honoring the sacrifice and preserving the legacy of our nation's heroes. Each year, we host the **National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C.** , bringing Americans together in a powerful display of remembrance and patriotism. We also proudly produce **" American Valor: A Salute to Our Heroes,"** a nationally televised tribute to the men and women who have served across generations.

But our work goes far beyond public events. At the heart of our mission is a commitment to **preserve the stories of veterans from every era of service** -- from the final voices of World War II, to those who served in Korea, Vietnam, and the post-9/11 generation. Through these efforts, we ensure that future generations understand the cost of freedom and the courage it has taken to defend it.

This year, American Veterans Center is marking historic military milestones: the 250th anniversaries of the U.S. Army, Navy, and Marine Corps...the 80th anniversary of the victories that won World War II...and key events in the Korean War 75 years ago, and the Vietnam War which ended 50 years ago this year.

name: Dr. Kristin Hook
subject: Continuing MLK's Legacy for Social Justice
body:
The arc of the moral universe is long, but it bends toward justice.

| | | | | [|
---](https://drkristinhook.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fd888d2bb4a2d4cad917af4b9&id=f2b247a7f4&e=395a33a3d2)
| | | | |
---
| | ,
Today we celebrate the legacy of Reverend Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. – whose message and activism still resonates as we continue the struggle for social and racial justice in America.
I see his legacy in the [people standing up to ICE in Hays County](https://drkristinhook.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fd888d2bb4a2d4cad917af4b9&id=f95fd68d77&e=395a33a3d2) after [agents injured someone in Kyle](https://drkristinhook.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fd888d2bb4a2d4cad917af4b9&id=a4b2814b47&e=395a33a3d2).
I see his legacy in the [volunteers showing up to feed Bexar County communities in need](https://drkristinhook.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fd888d2bb4a2d4cad917af4b9&id=48cb383610&e=395a33a3d2) when the government was shut down.
I see his legacy in [the helpers who showed up](https://drkristinhook.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fd888d2bb4a2d4cad917af4b9&id=a3a7d37574&e=395a33a3d2) in Kerr County to recover and rebuild a community devastated by the horrific flash floods on July 4th.
And I saw his legacy on display today in San Antonio – where [hundreds of thousands of people marched today](https://drkristinhook.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fd888d2bb4a2d4cad917af4b9&id=9d99afd62f&e=395a33a3d2) in unity to honor Dr. King’s life.
---
|
---
| |
I wish you and your family a restful and reflective holiday on all the work that has been done to build a more perfect union and the work that remains to ensure it is so.

https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ga-sept24?refcode2=7179520f-95f5-f011-8d4c-0022482d279b [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ga-sept24?refcode2=7179520f-95f5-f011-8d4c-0022482d279b]
Dear Friend,
Today, we honor the life and legacy of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. — a Georgian whose leadership, courage, and moral clarity continue to guide our work.
Dr. King reminded us that progress is not inevitable. It requires people willing to speak up, organize, and demand justice — especially when it is difficult or unpopular. His work challenged systems of inequality and called on leaders to act with courage, compassion, and accountability.
As the legislative session continues here in Georgia, those lessons remain as relevant as ever. This second week will focus largely on joint appropriations meetings beginning tomorrow, as lawmakers lay the groundwork for the debates, decisions, and votes that will resume next week.
House Democrats are entering this session committed to continuing the fight for strong public education, voting rights, democracy, affordability, and opportunity , and to standing up for communities that are too often left behind. We know that doing this work well means listening — not just speaking.
In the spirit of Dr. King’s legacy, I invite you to take a few moments — now or in the days ahead — to share which issues matter most to you and how you would like to stay engaged during this legislative session, if you haven’t already .
Thank you for being part of a movement rooted in justice, dignity, and opportunity for all.
In solidarity,
Leader Carolyn Hugley
Georgia House Democratic Caucus

name: Mark Ronchetti
subject: Why you can't get a doctor in New Mexico
body:
Plus: Kristi Noem just shut down CBS — "Yes it is 70%." | New for dpwillis67@gmail.com

| | | | | |
---
[|
---](https://nodoubtaboutitpodcast.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d2649c77b4f4f1f9d512804d2&id=bc5822e198&e=567664f14c)
| | | | | |
Can't get a doctor?
[There's a reason.](https://nodoubtaboutitpodcast.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d2649c77b4f4f1f9d512804d2&id=3350dc7175&e=567664f14c)
And it's not what they're telling you.
We follow the money on today’s all new episode of No Doubt About It!
---
[|
---](https://nodoubtaboutitpodcast.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d2649c77b4f4f1f9d512804d2&id=ba547b019c&e=567664f14c)
| |
💰 **$400 MILLION. ONE VERDICT.**
A New Mexico jury awarded $400 million in punitive damages in a single malpractice case.
That's why doctors leave. That's why insurance rates are insane. That's why you wait six months for a primary care appointment — and then they're gone before you even get seen.
Krysty went through two primary care doctors in six months. Same story you've probably lived.
The Albuquerque Journal called for reform. A group of trial lawyers fired back. Their solution? Taxpayer-funded subsidies for doctors — so lawyers can keep collecting massive verdicts.
Mark breaks it down: "The plumber and the teacher shouldn’t have to pay to bring doctors in so lawyers can keep getting rich."
---
| [Stream Episode Now](https://nodoubtaboutitpodcast.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d2649c77b4f4f1f9d512804d2&id=68d6752141&e=567664f14c)
---
| |
📺 **"IT'S NOT 70%." "YES IT IS."**
Kristi Noem went on CBS and said 70% of ICE detainees have violent charges.
Margaret Brennan's response? "It's not 70%."
Noem didn't flinch: "Yes it is. You guys keep lying and don't tell the public the truth." We play the clip. You need to see it.

📱 **BORROWED TRAUMA**
Krysty's friends in Minnesota did an experiment.
They took the viral social media posts about ICE raids — the ones scaring people into staying home — and fact-checked them.
No reports backing them up. None. It's borrowed trauma. People are terrified of stories that aren't real. And the media keeps fueling it.
We break down how it works.

🏛️ **MEMPHIS VS MINNEAPOLIS**
Memphis was the murder capital of America per capita in 2023.
Republican governor. Democratic mayor. They worked together with federal agencies. Over 5,000 criminals arrested.
Result? Crime collapsed. Minneapolis has the same problem. But leaders there would rather fuel the fire than fix it.
Same crisis. Opposite leadership. Opposite results.
---
| [Stream Episode Now](https://nodoubtaboutitpodcast.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d2649c77b4f4f1f9d512804d2&id=be63b68a79&e=567664f14c)
---
| |
🇨🇦 **"NEW WORLD ORDER"**
Canada's Prime Minister went to China and asked for a "new world order" partnership.
Watch the face of the Saskatchewan Premier sitting next to him. Priceless.
Then Ontario Premier Doug Ford ripped him apart: "I call it the spy car."
**We play both clips.**

Hello – whenever someone asks me what the hardest part of being deployed to Afghanistan was, I tell them: _“Little Caesar’s Hot-N-Ready pizza.”_
I missed one of everything while I was deployed: One of every birthday, one of every holiday. Recitals and soccer games. I knew what I had signed up for, but I still missed my husband. I missed our five kids even more.
After I finally returned home to Colorado, we were driving back from church one day when my husband, Chris, suggested we stop and get two of those $5 pizzas from Little Caesar’s.
Sitting at our kitchen table, surrounded by the six most important people to me in the world, I couldn’t help but feel an immense sense of gratitude to finally all be together again, just enjoying a simple meal.
_“Wow,”_ I told my husband. _“This was a great idea.”_
Grabbing another slice, he had no idea that what he said next nearly broke my heart: _“Yeah, we do this all the time.”_
Suddenly, I realized that there were all these little things – these new family traditions – that not only had I not been a part of, not only had I missed, but I had no idea existed. I had sacrificed so much more than I even knew. And it killed me. It still does.
**I am running for Congress against Lauren Boebert because I know what sacrifice means. I know what service looks like. And Lauren Boebert doesn’t have a clue. She is not a patriot. She doesn’t understand our values, our struggles, or what it means to serve. And worst of all: She doesn’t care.**
Adam Frisch only lost to Lauren Boebert by 546 votes. It was the closest race in the entire country. Together, we can write the final chapter in Lauren Boebert’s embarrassing political career – but I need your help now to do it.

The events at Cities Church in Minneapolis were not a mere protest; they were an outright attack on the sacred right to worship. Disrupting a church service, intimidating congregants, including the elderly and children, and trampling on private property is lawless behavior. America's churches are not playgrounds for political theater or media stunts. They are sanctuaries, protected by the Constitution and sacred in our nation's history.

**January 19, 2026** **MONDAY NEWS DIGEST**
| | Dear Rocky Mountain Voice family,
_As we mark**Martin Luther King Jr. Day** , we remember Dr. King’s commitment to equal justice under the law, personal responsibility, and the founding promise that all Americans are created equal. His call to judge people by the content of their character — not the color of their skin — remains a timeless reminder of the ideals this country continues striving to uphold._
We want to start today with a brief update on the **Tina Peters case** , before turning to what is now fully underway at the Capitol.
As we reported late last week, Peters’ appeal is heading into a critical phase, with [oral arguments complete](https://link.email.joinrmv.) and awaiting a decision with multiple legal questions still unresolved. Since then, additional concerns have emerged about her treatment inside the prison system, including [reports that she has again been placed in isolation](https://link.email.joinrmv.) following an altercation with another inmate. While the legal process continues, these developments have intensified scrutiny around both her custody status and the broader handling of the case. We’ve linked our latest reporting and outside commentary below for readers who want to follow the details as the court weighs its next steps.
◾️ [“You don’t get to ride both horses”: Appeals court presses both sides in Tina Peters case](https://link.email.joinrmv.) ◾️ [Griswold, county clerks urge Polis to reject clemency for Tina Peters ahead of appellate arguments](https://link.email.joinrmv.) ◾️ [What Really Happened with Tina Peters? Why are so Many Coloradans Calling for Her Release?](https://link.email.joinrmv.) [James Wiley on Free State Colorado] ◾️ [Mark Cook's Commentary on Oral Arguments](https://link.email.joinrmv.) [@PatriotMarkCook]
**Now, to the Capitol — where the 2026 legislative session is moving quickly.**
In the first days of session, House Democrats rolled out their [initial slate of bills](https://link.email.joinrmv.), signaling priorities that include housing, labor, and consumer protections. As is often the case, the early messaging has focused on affordability and cooperation, even as the details suggest expanded mandates, regulatory reach, and long-term costs that are [not always obvious on first read](https://link.email.joinrmv.). Several of our reports this week dig into what fiscal notes say — [and what they leave out](https://link.email.joinrmv.) — as lawmakers advance proposals with [“minimal impact” labels](https://link.email.joinrmv.) that counties and local governments may ultimately have to absorb.
That context matters when looking at [Jared Polis’ final State of the State address](https://link.email.joinrmv.), which struck a familiar tone. Polis highlighted economic growth and legislative accomplishments, while also casting Colorado as a victim of national political headwinds. Critics, meanwhile, point to persistent cost pressures, a growing structural budget gap, and the consequences of one-party control under the gold dome.
As this session unfolds, the tension between rhetoric and reality is already apparent. Bills are moving quickly, fiscal assumptions are being tested, and local governments are once again bracing for policies designed at the state level with real-world implications on the ground. **See our new _Legislative Session_ tab below and in every edition of the Mountain Minute for updates in real time!**
We’ll continue covering the session closely — not just the headlines, but the mechanics of how legislation actually works, what it costs, and who ultimately pays.
Thanks for reading and staying engaged as Colorado’s political year gets fully underway.
— Team RMV

name: The Democratic Party
subject: One year in…
body:
---
Derek, Tomorrow, we’ll officially be one year into Trump’s second presidency. **And, in just a few months, we face our most consequential midterm election yet — one that will determine whether our democracy remains intact in 2028.** Consider the damage Trump and his allies have done in the last 12 months:
* Spent millions of taxpayer dollars on deploying federal troops to American cities.
* Permitted the detention of lawful residents and the use of violence against American citizens.
* Cut funding for necessary agencies, projects, and services, firing tens of thousands of federal workers in the process.
* Gutted Medicaid, leaving millions of Americans unsure of where and how they’ll get health care for themselves and their families.
* Urged Republicans to redraw their congressional districts to rig this year’s midterms in his favor.
* Threatened to eliminate mail-in voting, challenged the independence of the FEC and longstanding campaign finance rules, and more in an attempt to dismantle our free and fair elections.

Derek, we know the year was overwhelming and disheartening. But all hope is not lost — we can and will fight back. **The first step? Winning back our Democratic congressional majority this November.** In 2025, voters showed up all over the country, with Democrats winning or overperforming in nearly 90% of key races. That didn’t happen by accident. Last year, we invested in Democratic state parties, held town halls, and organized _everywhere_. Now, we have to ramp up that work. **We just launched our largest-ever partisan voter registration program, a seven-figure investment in registering the next generation of Democratic voters.** We’re continuing to invest in every single state party and organizing on the ground to make sure voters across the country are ready to turn out this November. [**Derek, we know that none of this is possible unless all of us work together. name: Christopher Ahuja for Congress
subject: MLK and Stepping Forward When It Matters Most.
body:
Leadership stands up for what's right.

| | | | | [|
---](https://chrisahuja.us2.list-manage.com/track/click?u=67424df89870d1cac00e55f46&id=583ee0f373&e=53c7d12fc7)
| | | | | | Dear Peter,
Chris Ahuja here, Candidate for Congress in California’s 32nd District, Los Angeles.
As we honor Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. today, a leader who reshaped the moral imagination of a nation, I’m reaching out at a moment of profound instability in America.
This campaign is about protecting fundamental freedoms, defending democracy, and restoring truth and decency in public life.
It’s about lifting up working families, confronting extremism, and building a country where every person, regardless of background, has the opportunity to thrive. It’s about rebuilding trust in government at a time when that trust has been badly shaken.
I’ve spent my career as a small business owner committed to strengthening our Los Angeles community, always guided by the belief that leadership should be about people, not politics.
**I’m stepping forward now because Washington needs voices grounded in integrity, inclusion, and moral courage. Too many have chosen silence, appeasing the hate and rage politics of Donald Trump and the Republicans.**
It’s time to call out the strategic silence of 30-year incumbents like Brad Sherman. He claims to oppose ICE enforcement, yet when the administration ramps up raids and Congress pushes through enforcement funding, he disappears.
When Republicans introduced the outrageous Charlie Kirk Remembrance Day Act, comparing Kirk to Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., Sherman wouldn’t even take a stand. He voted “present,” choosing political safety over moral courage.
No pushback. No pressure. No fight.
That’s complicity, and a legacy of a politician who’s grown comfortable in his seat, not someone fighting for working families.
Brad Sherman’s actions have directly supported policies that hurt families, tear communities apart, and betray the public trust. Too often he has sided with Trump and Republican agendas, hoping voters will just keep on voting for him.
Our communities deserve leaders who tell the truth, stand up for justice, and act in the people’s interest. This is a moment that demands courage and relentless action. I’m ready to fight, and I hope you will stand with me to ensure the spirit of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. isn’t just honored today, but lived every day in America.

---
| |
**With determination,**[](https://chrisahuja.us2.list-manage.com/track/click?u=67424df89870d1cac00e55f46&id=561a7663bb&e=53c7d12fc7)**Chris Ahuja****Democratic Candidate for Congress, CA-32**

body:
https://maxinefororegon.com/ [https://maxinefororegon.com/]
Today, as we honor Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., we’re reminded that our fight for justice has always been about doing the work. He inspired us with a vision of a world where dignity and equality for all were a reality and made it very clear that for that dream to be realized, we had to be strategic, disciplined, and persistent in doing the work every single day.
That was apparent this afternoon at the Urban League of Portland’s MLK Day Brunch event, where Congresswoman Dexter gathered alongside hundreds of Oregonians to honor MLK’s fight for a more just nation—a fight that is as salient as it was 60 years ago.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_med_email-26q1?refcode=x_260119_MLK_act [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_med_email-26q1?refcode=x_260119_MLK_act] https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_med_email-26q1?refcode=x_260119_MLK_act [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_med_email-26q1?refcode=x_260119_MLK_act]
When the news cycle feels as heavy as it has lately, it’s easy to lose sight of Dr. King’s message that, together , ordinary people have the power to create extraordinary change.
That’s why it’s more important than ever for us to use every tool that we have available, including peaceful protests and holding elected officials accountable, to demand systemic change that honors the dignity of every person, no matter their race, gender, income, zip code, or immigration status.
So, Peter, please take today as a recommitment to your community, to one another, and to the ongoing work of making our democracy more just, more inclusive, and more humane.
That work has never been easy, but it has always, always been worth it.
In solidarity,
Team Dexter

While Most Nutmeggers enjoyed a Federal Holiday to honor the life of Martin Luther King Jr, a man who had a dream of Equality over bureaucratic "equity", Governor Ned Lamont directed the Office of Policy and Management to revert the land use values for farms and open spaces to their 2020 Rates averting tax increases for some farmers over 2300% ([See previous article](https://substack.com/redirect/54c3478d-dd8f-4b24-943a-84b46c999f86?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
## **Let 's Be Clear - This Did Not Happen By Action **
This reversal by Lamont was no accident. It was prompted due to a petition circulated that reached over 20,000 petitions in just a few days in a grassroots uprising of farmers, landowners, residents and neighbors standing up for the injustice to their friends and neighbors. _This is a beginning - It is Not a victory lap._
## **IF YOU HAVE NOT SIGNED THE PETITION ? DO 3 Things**

## Do Not Let Ned and Hartford Rewrite the Grassroots Narrative
It is really important that you stay on top of our elected officials, especially at the top of the ticket with Gov. Ned Lamont.
He will likely claim he listened and saved the farmers while it was his party that arrived at another detrimental piece of legislation that would have paved the way for forced sales, commercial farms, and conversion of farmland to 8-30g or other "affordable" housing wastelands.
**Without sustained pressure, this pause becomes a pivot --and the bulldozers return.**
## A Warning from History (and Music)
If we let up now, Connecticut's farmland future looks a lot like the warning sung decades ago by **Big Yellow Taxi** :
_**don't it always seem to go
that you don't know what youve got til its gone
they paved paradise
and put up a parking lot**_
**Do Not Rest on Your Laurels while we have made an impact to put Lamont and the one-party rule on the ropes (at least for a moment. Again - 3 Steps to Take Action and be informed and keep on Pressing:**

Pete Hegseth decided he's going to censure me, and is threatening to demote me and reduce my pension. I got shot at in service to this country. I missed holidays and birthdays. I commanded a space shuttle mission and launched to the International Space Station while my wife recovered from a gunshot wound to the head. My rank and retirement are things that I earned through my service and sacrifice for this country. Generations of servicemembers have done the same. Pete Hegseth wants to send a message to every single one that he will come after them if they say something he doesn’t like. You swear an oath to the Constitution when you join the military — including the First Amendment right to free speech. We swore to defend the foundational principles of this country. He is not going to stop me from defending our democracy from a president who is hellbent on destroying it. If they think this is going to shut me up, they’ve got another thing coming. ## Train Crash in Spain Kills at Least 40
At least 40 people were killed and [159 injured](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGOrDAQRE9jMlDb5hscOPgJ2Wy6IWpwM_TK2Ahag-b2K-YKm5X0pCq9-n6MD-TE-fmFGwVZypjpOhOJ0DEuKJjkQM5zSYlPLplzZMyjAeNq0LWBMSKn99hWMSxEhmxFQXeu99BZo6s1dK53k-0tousXq9H7qdMaIvyL7aJhrjjcbaANaA299Q36bvLe2dZZmMGCaoEiSzman8JZVlrSu7zoaOayVSmsIvup7H9lBmWG67qaeTpvi5srM9xRmeHckXP9sakjHchpoyx1JJT15tUR4n7x7ek61cJzQ06fCfnTL69gfgMAAP__9dl2wg) when two high-speed trains collided Sunday near Adamuz in southern Spain after one derailed and crossed onto an adjacent track. A train carrying 289 passengers from Málaga to Madrid [went off the rails](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO3CAURb8Gd1gPHsbjgiJSZCnFpk1pYfOw34aBESY7mr-PPL-w9ZWuzjl_PpYPz4nz_tvfybVYlkzPM1FrVJfom0-tes5bSYlPLplzYJ8XDdpKUFLDEjyn12K64CKRJuzIqdHeJhhRq-5wZt1wRRyC1REGhXEy4xZwsBtEY262Y3e9gdKgFNxw6v00rtNk0ViEDRCEAQrcSu0_C-d2UEyv8kW138q9S-5o7XEK_CH0LPTs1-0y6PdyzULPv3Kjmn3jkn0SetZK_uWUKEgFIDl__qsUpI-Nqjx4P-T5IAryrS30fLZSXwJnDgJ_Kj0hDiNCV114PPmKYkdhYL97Tm-e9q2IX07_DwAA___x54Px) at 7:45 p.m. and slammed into an incoming train with nearly 200 passengers traveling from Madrid to Huelva. The impact sent carriages plummeting down a 13-foot slope, with some bodies found hundreds of feet from the crash site as passengers were thrown through windows. This [video was recorded inside the Spanish train](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuwyAQhp8Gb7GOwxgzMHTxlq4drQuck6sIRA6Km7ev3Ffo9ku_9Enf93VeziRZyvWT7hzaWpfC-zNza7wtKzXKbSMpseYsT6lFShIqCwKOJ9AnhCWR5PcydCmszMim46DdOHlwBnV3C-A5UUwUrRkSJWe1cdFGu6JFb93USThooBG0hsn4nry7eD-aYTQQwYAagJO0uvXfVUq78Zrf9cVbH-u9y-HW2uOpzIfCWeG873t_ucTjUzgfMgrnlySux4gT2_cIw4-91m4L6bHLITY6NcD1TpL_mO1fIV4BfwMAAP__Gc5wgw) as passengers evacuated. Spanish Transport Minister Óscar Puente said the cause remains unknown but called it "extremely strange" because it occurred on a [straight, recently renovated](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGypCAQRb8GM6agUZSAYBOzt-mGVivt2FsMWMA-a_5-y_mFl986dc_587V8IUdOz9_4It_2vCS6aqTWqCw7NoytIKctx8iVc-IUGNMCCqxUWoJaAnJ8L30X_E4EZDryerSTU6MB3R0-mB3WfpimHZ3qR2etMoMd-qDNhrC6jv1NUxqU1moy7oFuXJ2zprdGbcoo0SsK3HJ5_M2c2kF7fOdvKo8tv7roj9bOKswvAbOA-bquB_0r-da4BwLmGy9gVlrArCcBMzYZCWuTgwyEQeLeqMh2ZVlPTFwPefDzkPUkCvLjX-WnQCDJSW65hLxiV3w4L77D2FH06vlCjp9P7Uchvz38DwAA___DRoY1) stretch of track, with both trains traveling under the speed limit.
## Winter Storm Threatens South
A powerful winter storm brewing in the Southwest could deliver [widespread snow and ice](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGypCAQRb8GM6ag9akEBJuQvU03tBCbsbcQLOgZa_5-y_2Fl3Ryuk7de_98L9-eEuXnb3-g5ViWjFdLyIx1iZ594uoph5ISNSqZ8kY-L6BglEpLUMvmKX2WodtsRATsO7R6Gmejph50t1sMJsSI66ZQQzDxa5iDDmb-UsPqA44d2dumNCit1dybhzfTaszYD2OvguqVGBRuxKU-_hbKvGNMn_LG-gjl6JLdmc8m-l8CnACXP2dpfCMB7hYLcEoLcNoIcK8m734CXCsv3tE3lqHcd60-UH7KWKo8y4U1vpK8KDNW2bjUQ_LuWV6Uklzr_dlyuaTPm6SAAlxX7XbemNo4iUE9D0_pf0T-0a5vC_8CAAD__9x1jX8) from Texas to the southeast coast by late this week after rare weekend snowfall blanketed parts of Florida, Alabama, and Georgia. The National Weather Service warns of a [potentially disruptive ice threat](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLtuwzAMRb_G3mTo4ZcGDV2ypWtHg5GomK0sBbISwX9fOFvnbsQhQdx7vq7LFShQvH_Chqb4tESse8BSMC8eCoSSgaJNIdBOKVJ0BHGRXI6MCyb54oDCsfStMx5RomrRiGmcNZ-UFO1qUA-9mkc5oxUSPA6TFxYUWi9vgwDVkjm_cSG5EHxWugM93bQeVT8qbrniTc_RUUm5-04Uy4o-HOmFubNpa4NZS3nsjfpo5KWRl1prF2_2bHHuT4JQVsznRLFgZn9BPlhF_GGwIji2PUOhR0CW0zO6ndkUHNtjqu8jjI5lG0EO_aR5m417VDrNjFPT8_sGFN6hyr9Mvoz8DQAA__8rI4nv) covering Texas, the Lower Mississippi and Tennessee valleys, and even parts of the mid-Atlantic and Washington, D.C. Wind chills this weekend are forecast to plunge to as [low as 40 to 50 below zero](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u2zAMhZ_G3mRIsuOfQUOXbOna0WBsKmYqi4HERsnbF765b3AXAvxAEOd8fy7zBShQvP2GHZ14niOWHFAE0-xBIEgCiguHQJk4UlwJ4my17ZU2yup5BQrvuatX5xEttjU6M_TjpIfWmnpz0BnwBifs4DRe9QjeW8DhZMD6EQeoyR3ftLHaGD22UwPTcJ2mvu36Vi-61VWncSXh1NyZomzow5ufmJqF9zq4TeSRq_ZXZc-VPZdSGs-vgiDb5-SAn00d3Sp7frBgFIKgdrhzUoWiYFJZOO3qmrBQvClYEuesMv-TTfnEuxJ8wTdAyKIWPmYAQVUQ_9bJrY9Ch6h-qDp924HCV0b5kdins_8DAAD__wH5ke8) in some areas, potentially marking the coldest air of the entire season. Meteorologists caution it's still too early to predict exact precipitation amounts but call the pattern a classic setup for disruptive icing.

body:

Peter,
First: Donald Trump handed down orders for red states to redraw their congressional districts to target and ruthlessly eliminate as many Democratic blue seats in their states as possible. Texas, Missouri, and North Carolina immediately passed newly gerrymandered maps.
Then: in a shocking and unexpected development, Indiana lawmakers rejected Trump's aggressive push to redraw their congressional map.
Now: Trump and his henchmen are pledging fire and fury for GOP lawmakers who defied them in Indiana, applying maximum pressure in the hopes they will flip and vote to eliminate another 1-2 blue seats there.
---
| [](https://6s79z9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001L2uqBGQmG0fV88pK47IRvUX-jDN-UgIj-mV6nAJN-o_oojNC4DMHLnjlOm7X85dppS0bKym0dk82PQqyI5zxA28sesBsCc5CYKkS2JOyB-ML7HrFYJj72Y0ZInN5Ki82mRpRbkmDtAQWzl29eI-emTHl98EE2a43hiJRGRNlIwVVKuzvbfiJCpTMLJSlxQqOlbJhTFE-3qhVgzsYcEjFrlLCTaq9h0dD&c=i3XHjHdG1Rm7WghzYp-cbv2AXwRqkeXPs5XYz1YMY0AAE0WaVQf8CQ==&ch=eeHdsH7UjvTIbNexETWiA38hJ2Vv4zn66961im3UugvNSBzF8tJ9FQ==)

Indiana could flip at any time. We need to keep working to counter any gains MAGA might make by pushing blue states to take up redistricting in response.
That's why Colorado Draws The Line is leading the ballot initiative that will allow Colorado Democrats to redraw their maps -- but our effort won't even get off the ground if we can't afford to place the issue before voters this year.
If Trump is willing to attack and bully his own party to win, imagine what he'll do to us. [We need you with us. We need to keep working to counter any gains MAGA might make by pushing blue states to take up redistricting in response. | | | | | == Peter, First: Donald Trump handed down orders for red states to redraw their congressional districts to target and ruthlessly eliminate as many Democratic blue seats in their states as possible. Texas, Missouri, and North Carolina immediately passed newly gerrymandered maps. Then: in a shocking and unexpected development, Indiana lawmakers rejected Trump's aggressive push to redraw their congressional map. Now: Trump and his henchmen are pledging fire and fury for GOP lawmakers who defied them in Indiana, applying maximum pressure in the hopes they will flip and vote to eliminate another 1-2 blue seats there. | == Things are moving fast now that both Trump and Vice President J.D. Vance are targeting Indiana GOP lawmakers with retribution if they don't fall in line and do what Trump wants. Indiana could flip at any time. We need to keep working to counter any gains MAGA might make by pushing blue states to take up redistricting in response. That's why Colorado Draws The Line is leading the ballot initiative that will allow Colorado Democrats to redraw their maps -- but our effort won't even get off the ground if we can't afford to place the issue before voters this year. | Amanda McKinney, a Yakima County Commissioner and candidate for Congress in Washington's 4th Congressional District, is dangerous. She is dangerous because she openly invites state violence into our communities and pledges loyalty to a President who has already turned that violence inward on the American people. What follows is why that matters.
America is a country of violence. We see ourselves as peacekeepers and generally good people, but the data suggests otherwise. No statistics are needed to recognize the horror that defines much of our daily life.
I lived for many years in Hong Kong, then one of the safest cities in the world. Despite its density, you would not hesitate to send your twelve-year-old daughter to the corner ATM at 2 a.m. to withdraw a thousand dollars and stop at a 7-Eleven on the way home for ice cream. The thought that harm might befall her did not exist because violence was absent from daily life, regardless of neighborhood. Living without fear changes you. It frees you to do more and to see the world through an optimistic lens. You do not recognize it at the time because it feels normal.
When I returned to the United States, it took nearly six months to feel comfortable again. I immediately felt the presence of violence. Living in a relatively safe part of West Valley, Yakima, I did not witness violence firsthand, but I was saturated by it through radio, television, newspapers, and social media. Whether through real accounts of gun violence or relentless political discourse, the weight was palpable. Over time, that fear became normalized, woven into daily life. I often wonder how our tolerance for violence would change if Americans could experience life without it, even briefly.

The evil has landed
Most of us have heard of Brian Heywood and his onslaught of questionably constitutional propositions he has tried to force onto Washington State ballots. He heads up the[ Let's Go Washington PAC](https://zmhksxhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001GS4EeHzBi73c6j1HVwwV7P3q9qfOKj3zJoX4nCQioOReb3kOHww9otn4g735XCChW3cNR2b4D1hRyhPQm4gWeK7sxanr7UQyH5fUQ3G5_32TeydxMV-vM9D847Jz1Qu_sUif72bWULT_nMQXAxooScBW0uA7IuzKXy7fHc4oJCV2iFiONnl-NKRqQCyybXR1&c=Rf79yU_Ko6C4MCmNg10O_s0Aj5clZGpEmu2esGnB6tiqzcpqoSoS-g==&ch=86rsToPIE_SZK4zX3Dwvo3RuUUqITDHVE_-_KmYrjVvzB4akBpncgw==), which was originally created to place six initiatives on the Washington ballot. Since then, with the help of several very wealthy Washingtonians, it has proliferated into another PAC, Washington Rising*. An odd name for a PAC registered in Tennessee, but less odd once you follow the money behind it.
According to the Washington State [PDC](https://zmhksxhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001GS4EeHzBi73c6j1HVwwV7P3q9qfOKj3zJoX4nCQioOReb3kOHww9otn4g735XCCh5Kmb4HKfTWUJTqGO4_iBvWD2UQUDGje0OOP4pu7G_oqF4DVVJ0e_YBSyKl6lzroP5sj-NOfoeNTdnPfcBqTyJw9XjsofSP_EYO9uudhRuunyt2oPEgkOkGe3UmZat27a7MGxJuUDdx0RHnkh1NziJp-vgMJDSofXSdFSPbT8Elw=&c=Rf79yU_Ko6C4MCmNg10O_s0Aj5clZGpEmu2esGnB6tiqzcpqoSoS-g==&ch=86rsToPIE_SZK4zX3Dwvo3RuUUqITDHVE_-_KmYrjVvzB4akBpncgw==), $1,074,999 has been donated by Washington residents, with $1,000,000 coming from just two donors, the Plath family and Robert Ramsey. The Plath family is behind the Washington Fruit and Produce Company and [Ramsey](https://zmhksxhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001GS4EeHzBi73c6j1HVwwV7P3q9qfOKj3zJoX4nCQioOReb3kOHww9otn4g735XCChoNTpujsZh6AG5YcMC9kkM-7WhuzfYs6M3v99VqcQF3dV5uTKbG5y69Jo8p8D_-z2IbTs8u7Sc_-v5XHy6RWr8JP8R6ATPUbEYjj5Ekd9oDd08l713m8KMKn9iO_CLDlBX7gqDplgPyeYqoZDVpAsMWMniF5Nm1lgVtx46-poqMPZiQqb7IzRbWucXukLeg0w0ahVKf9fFqg=&c=Rf79yU_Ko6C4MCmNg10O_s0Aj5clZGpEmu2esGnB6tiqzcpqoSoS-g==&ch=86rsToPIE_SZK4zX3Dwvo3RuUUqITDHVE_-_KmYrjVvzB4akBpncgw==) made his money off of Tribal members, beginning with the Yakima Nation. Knowing that the Yakima Nation and the Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation vote heavily Democratic, it is striking that people who profit from these communities would work seemingly against their interests.
That alone would be sufficiently scandalous to warrant scrutiny, but that is not my point.

She is dangerous because she openly invites state violence into our communities and pledges loyalty to a President who has already turned that violence inward on the American people. What follows is why that matters. America is a country of violence. We see ourselves as peacekeepers and generally good people, but the data suggests otherwise. No statistics are needed to recognize the horror that defines much of our daily life. I lived for many years in Hong Kong, then one of the safest cities in the world. Despite its density, you would not hesitate to send your twelve-year-old daughter to the corner ATM at 2 a.m. to withdraw a thousand dollars and stop at a 7-Eleven on the way home for ice cream. The thought that harm might befall her did not exist because violence was absent from daily life, regardless of neighborhood. Living without fear changes you. It frees you to do more and to see the world through an optimistic lens. You do not recognize it at the time because it feels normal. When I returned to the United States, it took nearly six months to feel comfortable again. I immediately felt the presence of violence. Living in a relatively safe part of West Valley, Yakima, I did not witness violence firsthand, but I was saturated by it through radio, television, newspapers, and social media. Whether through real accounts of gun violence or relentless political discourse, the weight was palpable. Over time, that fear became normalized, woven into daily life. I often wonder how our tolerance for violence would change if Americans could experience life without it, even briefly. | | == | Stephen Miller giving unlimited power to ICE Now we live under a new threat, one that comes from our own government acting against its own people. This is the danger we associate with Selma, Kent State, or the Bonus Army, moments when state power was turned inward. Those moments were horrific and limited. Today, the threat is broader and more sustained. Our President has turned state violence inward with deliberate force. Washington, D.C., Los Angeles, Chicago, Portland, Memphis, New York City, Baltimore, New Orleans, Oakland, San Francisco, St. Louis, and most recently Minneapolis. In the span of a single week, one person was killed and another shot. The response was not restraint or remorse, but escalation. According to == there are as many as 3,000 troops on standby to deploy to Minnesota under a manufactured narrative of immigration and domestic terrorism. ICE, as intended, provides a necessary service. As it exists today, it has become an army of terror directed at the American people. With warrantless stops, Kavanaugh-era standards, and absolute immunity, the incentive appears to be escalation. Violence is the only argument where more is required to achieve less. In Washington, we have largely avoided the President's direct threat. Even Yakima County's Constitutional Sheriff, Bob Udell, has said his office would not support ICE raids. Yet we have traitors in our ranks. Amanda "MAGA Barbie" McKinney petitioned to bring federal troops into our towns. Amanda has pledged singular loyalty to the President and is the single greatest threat to our community's safety. Amanda has moved beyond rhetoric. She has == for the kind of violence now playing out in Minneapolis. If elected, Amanda would bring armed personnel into our streets under the guise of public safety. She is dangerous. Because of people like Amanda McKinney, Rural Americans United will not stop. | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

name: MassDems
subject: Gov. Healey and LG. Driscoll just announced their re-election campaign TODAY!
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Massachusetts Democratic State Committee
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP31/1/93809/images/Logo.png]
Hey Democrats!
Gov. Healey and LG. Driscoll just announced their re-election campaign TODAY with a brand new launch video [https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1DUgEQGCpN/] that we’d love for you to share.
We’d also love your help spreading the word with these sample social media posts and graphics. You’re welcome, of course, to change any of the language to make the posts feel more personal to you.
Your help is greatly appreciated to help us continue to build the momentum we need to win — and win big — on Election Day.
SAMPLE LANGUAGE FOR SHARING: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/166veZcOJ_Z4fr70hV3uA_0Lp2t7FKthxA5Fk-LzX0po/edit?usp=sharing]
* Just my two cents: Massachusetts is better off with Maura Healey and Kim Driscoll leading the way. 💙
* Gov. Healey’s on a winning streak: she eliminated broker's fees, capped health care co-pays and deductibles (for the first time ever), and is building 100,000 new homes. I’m so proud to support her reelection campaign.
* Gov. @maura_healey is always going to stand up to anyone who tries to get in Massachusetts’ way, including Donald Trump. That’s the kind of leadership we need now more than ever.
* While Donald Trump is raising costs, taking away our health care, and tearing families apart, the Healey-Driscoll administration is protecting what matters in Massachusetts. I couldn’t be more excited that they’re running for another term!
* The best ballers know how to play good offense and defense. That’s what we get with @maura_healey and @kimdriscollma. And I know that they’re always going to keep standing up for what’s right.
* First as Attorney General and now as Governor, @maura_healey has devoted her career to improving people’s lives. She’s the leader we need to stand up to Trump and move Massachusetts forward. I can’t wait to vote for her again this year.
* Let’s go!!! Governor Healey and Lieutenant Governor Driscoll have our backs, and now it’s time to have theirs.
* I’m really proud that here in Massachusetts we have a Governor and Lieutenant Governor who show up and do the work. I’m ready for 4 more years!
* It feels good to have leaders I actually trust to put people first. Grateful for Maura Healey and Kim Driscoll — and fired up to reelect them!
* Proud to call Massachusetts home because here, we have leaders who deliver. Couldn’t be more excited to support Gov. Healey and Lt. Gov Driscoll’s campaign for reelection.
* I believe leadership matters — and I’m glad our state has leaders who care and who listen. And I’m ready to help them win again in November!
* With so much chaos in D.C., I’m thankful that we have a governor and lieutenant governor who are standing up for Massachusetts and getting things done. Let’s go @maura_healey and @kimdriscollma!
* Donald Trump is attacking our values and coming after states like ours. That’s why we need to reelect a governor in Massachusetts we can count on to stand up for Massachusetts and fight back. That’s @maura_healey.
OR WRITE YOUR OWN:
The best way to support Maura and Kim is in your own words! If you want to draft your own post, here are some prompts to get you started:
* Why do you support Maura and Kim?
* What do you want your social media followers to know about what’s at stake in this election?
* How do your followers FEEL the positive impact of Maura and Kim’s leadership every day?
You could even turn your responses to the questions above into a selfie-style video. People want to hear from you!
GRAPHICS TO USE: DOWNLOAD THEM HERE [https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1SjlP36BVDgP_giND7iI2gW1-g0k9kOdB?usp=sharing]
https://docs.google.com/document/d/166veZcOJ_Z4fr70hV3uA_0Lp2t7FKthxA5Fk-LzX0po/edit?usp=sharing [https://docs.google.com/document/d/166veZcOJ_Z4fr70hV3uA_0Lp2t7FKthxA5Fk-LzX0po/edit?usp=sharing]
This work doesn’t happen without people like you stepping up, getting involved, and sharing their values. Because of supporters like you, we’re fighting for affordable lives, real opportunity, and standing up to the damage Donald Trump is doing each and every day.
P.S. If you want to sign up to volunteer with Team Healey-Driscoll, click here. [https://mobilize.us/s/NGHQeI]

# **Trump calls church protesters "professional insurrectionists," demands jail or deportation**
President Donald Trump blasted anti-ICE protesters who stormed a Minnesota church during Sunday's service as "professionals" who are "highly trained to scream, rant, and rave, like lunatics," **[demanding they be"thrown in jail,](https://substack.com/redirect/1619c9b0-71ef-4f7a-9d97-72a9d152c294?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** or thrown out of the Country" in an early-morning Truth Social post Tuesday, while the Department of Justice investigates the raid on Cities Church in St. Paul.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1619c9b0-71ef-4f7a-9d97-72a9d152c294?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Trump demands Walz and Omar be "first to go," calls for investigation:** Trump declared that Gov. Tim Walz and Rep. Ilhan Omar should be "first to go" and demanded "Investigate these Corrupt Politicians, and do it now!" after DHS shared video of the church protest and accused Walz and Minneapolis Mayor Jacob Frey of "whipping these mobs into a frenzy and then allowing them to run rampant," claiming protesters are "going from hotel to hotel, church to church, hunting for federal law enforcement."
* **Protesters targeted pastor allegedly moonlighting as ICE director:** The protest, which was joined by former CNN anchor Don Lemon, saw churchgoers harassed and stalked into the streets by demonstrators who called out resident pastor David Eastwood for allegedly working for ICE, with the pastor's personal information appearing to match that of the David Easterwood identified in court filings as the acting director of the ICE St. Paul field office who appeared alongside DHS Secretary Kristi Noem at a Minneapolis press conference in October.

* * *
# **Software engineers berated by anti-ICE mob during lunch**
A group of white male software engineers dressed casually in sweatshirts and jackets were eating lunch at Clancey's Deli in Minneapolis when one of them got an alert on an anti-ICE Signal chat telling members that plainclothes agents were at the restaurant, prompting **[dozens of anti-ICE agitators to flock to the restaurant](https://substack.com/redirect/83ef8ab3-11ac-4dad-a031-5ef5694e30dc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and peer into the window.

* **Crowd hurls insults, calls them "pedophiles" and "bootlickers":** After the group left, they were met on the street with derision from the crowd shouting "You're a f------ bootlicker b----!" and "Get out of our f------ neighborhood!" with Lee, one of the engineers, saying "Next thing we know, people are yelling, 'I hope you die,' and calling us pedophiles," while the crowd appeared unconvinced even after one man tried explaining "We do custom apps for a whole bunch of companies around Minnesota and the country."
* **Engineer politically aligned with anti-ICE cause shocked by attack:** The person who received the message on the "SW Minneapolis Rapid Response" chat is aligned politically with the anti-ICE cause, with Lee telling Alpha News "My friend was shocked. He's on the [anti-ICE] side politically. He lives nearby. He's eaten there before. And suddenly he's seeing messages saying we're ICE," while one engineer told the crowd "The way you guys are acting? No. And I don't support ICE either. I'm just trying to enjoy my lunch!"

# President Trump's first year back in review
President Donald Trump has been back in office for one year as of today, and his agenda has operated at warp speed **[to make America prosperous, healthy, secure, and great again.](https://substack.com/redirect/b92d13c7-d001-478e-8379-d3b87271ac6c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b92d13c7-d001-478e-8379-d3b87271ac6c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Trump 's tariffs drive historic trade deals and investments:** President Trump's "Liberation Day" worldwide tariff policy on April 2, 2025, generated tremendous leverage to negotiate deals, headlined by a historic July 27 agreement with the EU where they committed to purchase $750 billion in American energy and invest $600 billion in America while paying a 15% tariff, with Trump attracting $18 trillion in total investment to the U.S. in one year and striking Most-Favored-Nation deals with pharmaceutical companies that slashed drug prices by up to 1,400%.
* **Border security achieves record-low illegal immigration:** The Trump administration closed out 2025 with a historically low apprehension rate of less than 109,000 illegal aliens for the year, a 93% drop in border crossings, with DHS removing over 622,000 illegal aliens and 1.9 million self-deporting, while constructing 130,000 feet of temporary barriers and commissioning completion of Trump's border wall through the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.
* **Eight conflicts settled through "peace through strength" foreign policy:** Trump settled or de-escalated eight conflicts worldwide, including the historic October Middle East peace deal ending the Israel-Hamas war with all 20 living hostages released, a December 4 agreement ending three decades of conflict between the Democratic Republic of Congo and Rwanda, and operation "Absolute Resolve" on January 3 capturing Venezuelan dictator Nicolas Maduro without U.S. casualties, earning him the Inaugural FIFA Peace Prize and Maria Corina Machado's 2025 Nobel Peace Prize.
* **Economic boom with 5.3% GDP growth and historic tax cuts:** The Atlanta Fed projects 5.3% GDP growth in Q4 despite a 43-day Democrat shutdown, while Trump halted Biden-era inflation to just 1.6% core inflation over three months, presided over rising wages ($1,048 for typical private-sector workers, $3,336 for miners), and signed the One Big Beautiful Bill Act providing $191 billion in net new tax relief including $25,000 deductions for tipped workers and $12,500 for overtime workers.

Friends,
We are living inside a rapidly accelerating catastrophe.
My husband's unlawful detention, which has absorbed so much of our energy these past months, is a signal flare, yes, but the bonfire is already upon us.
Let me save you many hours, and name several trajectories that are converging on a place none of us want to go:
1. ICE is planning more camps. Well over a dozen of them.
2. Anecdotal evidence shared on social media months ago indicated that people with Hispanic last names had been deleted from government databases. What more convenient way to suddenly have "millions" of undocumented people than to delete the documents? (Is that part of what DOGE was up to?)
3. Already they are targeting protestors, peaceful observers, dissidents with violence, including murder.
4. Already the murderers are told loud and clear they have full immunity.
5. Already Palantir is tracking, logging, and analyzing all of our digital activity - as well as our license plates, faces, and Ring cameras.
6. The threat to Greenland - which, as of this writing, looks like it will resolve into military force very soon (I've seen testament that military bases are hiring medical staff in preparing for an influx of wounded, and Trump activating the Alaska-based military battalion is - obviously - not actually intended for Minnesota) - will very probably be the straw that breaks the camel's back.
1. Immediately, Article 5 of NATO is activated: against the United States, the leading member. A diplomatic and economic disaster, however the military angle shakes out. Europe has plenty of economic pressure to bring to bear.
2. Canada - Canada! - has signed a new strategic alliance with China _and_ indicated in public that if the US touches Greenland, Canada will ally itself with Europe. And open hostilities. Against the United States. With whom it shares over two thousand miles of border.
3. Watch the logic, in targeting dissidents:
1. As soon as war, or hostilities of any kind, are declared against the United States, then this country has enemies. Invading Greenland is 100% guaranteed to instantly turn our best allies into our enemies.
2. But once the United States has enemies, then **anyone within the borders of the United States who supports them** (and how generous do we think Noem and Bondi will be in their definition of the word "support"?) will be, by legal definition, a traitor.
3. Treason is punishable with death.
4. Ergo, if you think it is wrong for the US to invade Greenland, and you think Greenland and Europe are justified in fighting back, congratulations, you'll be suddenly branded a traitor.
5. If your online activity also indicates anything they might justify as "anti-American" or "anti-Christian," congratulations, you're already well on your way to being branded a "domestic terrorist" under NSPM-7 - but as we all know, a peaceful mother of 3 who was turning her car around in the vicinity of ICE agents was branded a "domestic terrorist," so who knows what it means anymore--
1. except the inimitable Caitlin Johnston, who said a long time ago that "Terrorist is an Empire term that simply means 'disobedient population that needs bombs dropped on them'." Always appreciate her clarity.
7. Trump and this regime are now _openly_ invoking Nazi messaging - actual, honest Nazi messaging - in their public facing communications, propaganda videos, even the placard on Noem's podium in a recent press conference. "All of yours for one of ours" for instance, is a direct Nazi quote: if a Nazi soldier was killed, they killed every person in that village.
8. There are major financial currents at play that will functionally wreck the US dollar within this year, perhaps within months.
1. The Federal Reserve is printing money again. That will drive down everyone's purchasing power (eg, drive up inflation). Every dollar will be worth less. It may happen fast.
2. With the AI bubble and massive overleveraging at the core of the stock market, it is entirely possible we will see another '08 level crash - or worse - this year. Maybe this season.
3. BRICS has implemented new financial rails to settle international transactions: an independent alternative to the SWIFT banking system run out of the USA, that has until just now been the operating standard for every country on earth.
1. As other countries - rightfully wary of the United States - move to start settling their debts and transactions on a system the United States doesn't control, expect more financial and monetary damage to the US as we are simply routed around as the proven-volatile and untrustworthy actor any sane person would want to cut out of their business dealings.
4. Europe, China, and Canada all hold huge amounts of US Treasury bonds. Their holding of those bonds is what is propping up our economy. If they dump them, our economy is toasted. Pretty darkly so. Nice and crispy. "Greater recession" level harm is not impossible, in this scenario.
9. Meanwhile, credible reporting from a career CIA officer tells us that the only reason Trump bombed Iran in 2025 is that Israel threatened that if the United States did _not_ bomb Iran, Israel would use nuclear weapons. The same officer told viewers that after thirty years of working for the agency, he had seen every president, of every administration and party, be approached by Israel and pressured to bomb Iran. Every one had said no; until this threat, which Trump responded to.
10. Relatedly, the recent mass protests in Iran were infiltrated by violent non-state actors - widely acknowledged to be tied to Mossad - who incited violence and caused property damage, in an attempt to provoke force and/or stir up mass agitation. Credible reporting indicates that the Mossad networks that just become exposed in these protests had been cultivated for decades to conduct a regime-change operation in Iran. And that now, with their exposure, that "strategic asset" for the United States (and Israel) is destroyed. No longer usable. And thousands are dead.
11. The AI targeting systems that have been used to identify targets in Gaza - and kill them, without a human being ever involved - have been sold back to the United. States, I am sorry to say.
12. Those AI targeting systems can be seamlessly fused with all of our Flock/Ring/cell phone/location data, to execute arrests.

I don't like where this is going.
If you **learned** something here that was valuable to you,
please subscribe, like and share.
Thank you.
Stay safe out there .

body:
#

[
---
See, I get why some folks voted for Trump. He promised to attack a broken system. And it’s a ripe target. Even before Trump came on the scene, America had one of the most corrupt political systems in the Western world. It’s been running on corporate money, secret money, billionaire money. And it’s worse than ever now. _Citizens United_ was the worst court decision in modern American history. When members of Congress aren’t begging for money from Washington lobbyists, they’re trying to dodge getting carpet-bombed by super PACs. Senators get threatened with millions of dollars of attack ads over the votes they take. And see, _that_ is why things don’t work for ordinary people. It’s because the people’s elected representatives don’t represent the people. They represent the big donors! _That corruption is why they defunded nursing homes to cut taxes for the rich._ _Corruption is why you pay a fortune for prescriptions._ _Corruption is why your insurance claim keeps getting denied._ _Corruption is why hedge funds get to buy up all the houses in your neighborhood, and then your corporate landlord ignores your calls during a gas leak._ _Corruption is why that ambulance costs $3,000 after you just had to get your choking toddler to the hospital._ Yes, the system really is rigged. But Trump’s not unrigging it. He’s re-rigging it for himself! He’s a crook and a con man, and he wants to be a king. You can’t claim to be for ordinary men and women when you defund their hospitals and nursing homes. You can’t claim to be for ordinary men and women when you defund school lunch programs to help feed little boys and little girls whose hard-working parents are struggling to fill the fridge. You can’t claim to be for ordinary men and women when you do these things so you can cut taxes for the richest people in the country while you and your family business rake in massive sums from around the world. Donald Trump’s second term has already done unfathomable damage to our country and the lives of millions of people. And the people are beginning to see it. But only by regaining Congressional power can we stop him. _Really._ The upcoming 2026 midterms are our last chance to restore checks and balances. And my Senate race in Georgia is the single most critical contest: _I’m the only Democratic Senator up for reelection in 2026 in a state Trump carried in 2024._ **[So if you’re outraged by what’s happening to our country — and you’re ready to fight for the future of this Republic –– please don’t wait until 2028: Rush $5 to my reelection campaign in Georgia right now.**](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-jan26.wPRyEn&refcode=em260120-1-f&t=2&akid=1473%2E5691347%2EskYcap) Here’s the link to donate: **[https://act.electjon.com/go/donate](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-jan26.wPRyEn&refcode=em260120-1-f&t=3&akid=1473%2E5691347%2EskYcap)** The average online donation to our campaign is around $30. Please give what you can. All that matters is that lots and lots of people are contributing what they can to power our grassroots campaign. **[Please, contribute today.](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-jan26.wPRyEn&refcode=em260120-1-f&t=4&akid=1473%2E5691347%2EskYcap)** Jon Ossoff

subject: Barlow For Wyoming Newsletter
body:
B is for Barlow, Budget, Big Horn Basin and Bentonite
| | | | | | [ ](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01KFE13EKR9PBWRCCHS7753P5S_0)
---
| **Welcome to the Barlow for Wyoming Newsletter. Your hub for latest news, information and upcoming events.**
---
|
---
| | |
---
| B is for Barlow, Budget, Big Horn Basin, and Bentonite
---
| Hello friends, This week took us through the Big Horn Basin, where we spent time in Big Horn, Hot Springs, and Washakie Counties. Our visits even included a bit of lambing, helping me not miss home too much! Discussions of Wyoming’s mineral resources were fruitful, including a tour of bentonite operations. We appreciated the chance to visit with folks who care deeply about their communities and our state’s future. The hospitality was as generous as ever, with many stops including lunch at the Worland Senior Center. We are grateful to our local County Chairs and supporters, who helped arrange for friends and neighbors to join us for a week of events. These conversations and experiences continue to reinforce why practical leadership, respect for working people, and stewardship of Wyoming’s resources are essential, especially as we look ahead to making responsible cash-based budgeting and long-term fiscal decisions for our state. \- Eric
---
| **Ride with Barlow for Wyoming**
---
| Eric's campaign is powered by folks who believe in Wyoming’s values of hard work, integrity, and community. Your contribution keeps us moving forward to build a stronger future for our state. **👉 Join the ride — chip in today!**
---
| | [ DONATE ](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01KFE13EKR9PBWRCCHS7753P5S_1)
---
|
---
| | | | |
---
| Cash-based Budgeting: A Transparent, Stable Approach to State Budgeting In Wyoming, we don’t forget where public money comes from. It comes from the people who work hard. The folks who get up early, stay late, and do the jobs that keep this state moving. Those dollars come from families, workers, and businesses who expect their government to treat public money with the same discipline and respect they use at their own kitchen tables. As Governor, I will keep our budgets lean, efficient, and honest. That means we budget and spend what we actually have, not what we hope for. Families and small businesses plan within their means. They make decisions based on the income they can count on, not uncertain projections. Wyoming’s government should operate with that same discipline by grounding its budget with real dollars that are in the bank. Our current budgeting process is based on what we hope to collect. The Consensus Revenue Estimating Group (CREG) analyzes trends and estimates what we expect the state to receive in tax dollars. The Governor then proposes a budget, and the legislature makes its adjustments. Both use the CREG’s work product. While the CREG is diligent in its approach and conservative with its estimates, we can strengthen the state budgeting process by gradually building one to two years of cash reserves so the state’s budget is supported by money we already have. This approach is “cash-based budgeting.” When the government builds a budget on projections, we risk overcommitting in boom years and scrambling when revenues drop. A cash-based approach avoids those swings by ensuring every expense is backed by a real dollar, instead of shifting forecasts. Whether it is state or local governments, this is the kind of enhanced fiscal discipline and transparency people deserve from their government. Wyomingites want to know their money is spent responsibly, whether it comes from a sales tax receipt or earnings from our Permanent Mineral Trust Fund. Cash-based budgeting provides a clear guardrail against overspending by ensuring essential services are funded first and that any surplus is carefully evaluated for long-term need and sustainability.
Depending on the year, between 40 and 50 percent of Wyoming’s budget is funded by mineral and energy revenues, and those revenues can change quickly when markets shift. Another 20 to 30 percent is generated from investment income, which is also dependent on unpredictable markets. A cash-based system helps smooth out the highs and lows, allowing the state to save in strong years and maintain essential services during lean ones. Wyoming’s core industries will always rise and fall, but that doesn’t mean our budgeting should.
---
| **On The Trail**
---
|
---
| | | TEN SLEEP and THERMOPOLIS Our trip started over the mountain in Tensleep, where we had a nice meet-up with folks at the Daily Bread Cafe. Thank you to Aaron Anderson for arranging this for us, and thanks to Ed Cooper for joining us here and for other tours. Brooks Jordan and Chris Delay from Hot Springs State Parks, as well as Meri Ann Dorman from the local Chamber of Commerce, joined us for lunch to share an overview of Hot Springs State Park, and its importance to the region. We also did a walk-through with CEO Scott Alwin and board members John Anderson and John Fenton and team at Hot Springs Health, an important community anchor. While there, physicians showed us some innovative training programs they are using.
---
| | |
---
|
---
| | | | |
---
| We continued our journey the next day in Thermop with a meet-up at The Storyteller, where we had a great local turnout and some fun. We were glad folks from Meeteetse, Ten Sleep and the Wind River Canyon area were able to join. We continued to Big Horn Enterprises, where we learned about the impact of BHE's residential, community, and employment services for special needs citizens and their families. BHE also has operations in Worland and Powell.
---
|
---
| | | **WORLAND** In Worland, we stayed busy! We started with the Washakie Development Authority, talking about key Wyoming topics like Ag and Energy, as well as Washakie County's other important industries, including long-running Admiral Beverage and manufacturing companies like Crown Holdings and Unique Precision Industries. We also toured the Oxbow Center, which offers area citizens with mental health and substance abuse support. County Chairs and supporters Aaron Anderson, Ron and JaDee Harvey, Phillip and Shurie Scheel, and Tim and Jamie Flitner organized an evening meet-and-greet with area folks at the Washakie Museum and Cultural Center.
---
| | |
---
|
---
| | | GREYBULL
On the way to Greybull, we dropped by a lambing operation to chat with some folks who weren't able to make it to our meet-and-greet. I tried to talk them into adding some yak, but they said they were all set. In town, we met with Mayor Myles Foley, Councilman Gerald Crist, and Administrator Dawn Norton, who shared the great work Greybull is doing to recruit businesses to the community. Housing is a continuing issue, but some success has been achieved through state grants and loans. We toured the business park with Councilman Crist. A quick stop for a gift for Kelly at the Crazy Woman store and to say hi to Lori and Holton Harter. We discussed the importance of small businesses.
---
| | |
---
| | | | |
---
| | |
---
| | | Joe Sylvester and Jared Mowery with Wyoming Bentonite gave us a tour of the mine, which, in addition to being important to oil and gas development, also serves as the main component in cat litter. Our Wyoming Bentonite gets mixed, processed, and packaged here before being sent around the world. We sampled the bentonite by tasting it, which determines 'grit' quality. Confirmed!
---
| | |
---
|
---
| | | SHELL
We toured the Leavitt Reservoir in Shell with Expansion Project Board Members John Ed Anderson and Fred Barnett, and learned the expansion will increase the reservoir by 10-fold!. State dollars have supported this important project, a part of Governor Mead's '10-in-10' initiative. Water is critical to Wyoming, and we were fortunate to get a viewpoint from the ground up on this topic. The project is anticipated to be completed by late summer. We rounded out the tour with a meet-and-greet at the Shell Bar, arranged by Tim and Jamie Flitner. We appreciate the hospitality from Shell Bar owners Gene and Patty Elliot and their amazing crew. The space was beautiful, and the crowd was lively as they cheered on the Broncos and the Bills. We were sad for our own Josh Allen's eventual loss, but thrilled at Frank Crum's historic TD catch. As a group, we cheered on UW as a winner either way. The World Needs More Cowboys like Josh and Frank!
---
| | |
---
| |
---
|
---
| **Get In The Saddle**
---
| | |
---
| | | | Wyoming’s strength has always come from neighbors pitching in. Join the Barlow For Wyoming team of volunteers who are helping share his message across our state. **🤠 Ride with us — sign up to volunteer!**
---
