#### [**_3X MATCH ACTIVE:_**](https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/DzpWMVYqjEF-)
[**_RENEW YOUR LCV MEMBERSHIP FOR JUST $5 >>_**](https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/-)
---
| | **FIRST** , Trump shut down construction on clean energy projects that were already approved, funded, and moving forward — halting offshore wind along the East Coast and derailing power for millions of homes— in an escalation of his attempts to ban clean energy projects to unfairly advantage his fossil fuel donors.
---
| | **THEN** , he ordered aging coal plants in Colorado, Indiana, Michigan, and Washington to stay open, against the wishes of plant operators and local communities, who are now facing even more polluted air.
---
| | **NOW** , it’s up to the environmental movement to determine what happens next. LCV is working to rally opposition to Trump’s dirty energy agenda — on Capitol Hill, in communities across the country, and through grassroots pressure campaigns — but the truth is that the success of our campaigns depends on support from LCV members.
---
| | Our **2026 January Membership Drive** is underway, and through the end of this month, **your impact will triple.** [**_The best thing you can do to oppose Trump’s dirty energy agenda is to renew your LCV membership today. Right now, every $5=$15 in impact._**](https://links.messages.lcv.)
---
| | | [ RENEW WHILE EVERY $5=$15 >> ](https://links.messages.lcv.)
---
| | The pattern couldn’t be clearer: Trump is **blocking clean energy** like wind and solar and propping up the deadly fossil fuel industry — **rewarding the oil, gas, and coal executives** who fund his campaigns and staff his administration. And everyday people and communities are paying the price — through more polluted air and water and worse health outcomes.
---
| | That’s why your LCV membership is so important at this moment. We’re working not only to rally communities to push for clean energy, we’re also responding to each reckless Trump ploy to resuscitate the dying and costly coal industry. We can’t do it without your membership, Peter.
---
| | | [ RENEW WHILE EVERY $5=$15 >> ](https://links.messages.lcv.)
---
| | **Here’s how forcing coal plants to stay open is hurting people across the country: **
---
| | In Colorado, the Craig Generating Station’s Unit 1 was scheduled to be retired and was already offline due to a mechanical failure. Then Trump intervened, forcing it to continue running and polluting local communities.
---
| | This isn’t an isolated case. Similar orders have kept coal plants operating across the West and Midwest, creating a blueprint for locking in dirty, expensive energy and blocking progress toward a safer, more sustainable planet.
---
| | As we head deeper into 2026, the strength of the environmental movement depends on the size and commitment of LCV’s membership base. This moment calls for every single person who wants a more just, equitable, and sustainable future to step up — and it starts with people like you.
---
| | **Please don’t wait, Peter.** [**_Renew your LCV membership today for just $5 while your impact TRIPLES to help ensure that the voices and needs of everyday people, not corporate polluters, shape our energy future._**](https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/x_yzTg-)
---
| | Thank you for being part of LCV.

| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/123700075/596272109/-975735282?refcode=em_logoheader&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MjIyOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZGVkMDcyYy00MWY2LWYwMTEtOGQ0Yy0wMDIyNDgyZDI3OWIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=n65csAALoXAyI04C7yxLaViI-zNuPwDbStqhY7Szl4o=)

Peter,

Growing up, I never looked at politicians and thought, "That's what I want to be someday." What inspired me instead were the scientists who changed the world by caring deeply and taking risks for the greater good.

I remember learning about Dr. Jonas Salk, who developed the polio vaccine at a time when that disease was devastating families across the country — and who volunteered to be one of the first people to receive it himself. Or Dr. Marie Curie, whose groundbreaking discoveries made X-rays possible and gave doctors new tools to save lives. **These were people who saw a problem and chose to act.**

But what I admire most about those scientists isn't just what they discovered. It's the fact that they didn't settle for what already existed. They could have stayed comfortable in a lab and avoided risk. Instead, they answered a calling to improve the world around them.

I could nerd out about this for ages, but to make a long story short: that same instinct is what eventually led me to run for office.

I never planned to be a politician. But I looked around my community and saw neighbors I care about struggling because of decisions made far away from them. I saw families stressed about healthcare costs, about wages that don't keep up with expenses, about whether they could give their kids the life they dream of. I saw people working hard and still feeling like they were falling behind. And I couldn't stop thinking: we can do better than this.

I'm ready to be that change as a representative who listens first. I won't be scared to challenge what isn't working and work together toward real solutions.

**[That's the kind of leadership I want to bring to IA-01. If this vision resonates with you, I'd be honored to have you with me in this work. And if you're able, I hope you'll consider supporting our campaign by making a donation. Every dollar helps.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/123700076/596272110/-2011951990?refcode=em26_260120_scienc_fnd_gq_act___CB_ettx&utm_campaign=em26_260120_scienc_fnd_gq_act___CB_ettx&utm_medium=email&refcode2=3ded072c-41f6-f011-8d4c-0022482d279b&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MjIyOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZGVkMDcyYy00MWY2LWYwMTEtOGQ0Yy0wMDIyNDgyZDI3OWIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=n65csAALoXAyI04C7yxLaViI-zNuPwDbStqhY7Szl4o=)**

Thank you,

Christina

clean_body: | = Peter, Growing up, I never looked at politicians and thought, "That's what I want to be someday." What inspired me instead were the scientists who changed the world by caring deeply and taking risks for the greater good. I remember learning about Dr. Jonas Salk, who developed the polio vaccine at a time when that disease was devastating families across the country — and who volunteered to be one of the first people to receive it himself. Or Dr. Marie Curie, whose groundbreaking discoveries made X-rays possible and gave doctors new tools to save lives. These were people who saw a problem and chose to act. But what I admire most about those scientists isn't just what they discovered. It's the fact that they didn't settle for what already existed. They could have stayed comfortable in a lab and avoided risk. Instead, they answered a calling to improve the world around them. I could nerd out about this for ages, but to make a long story short: that same instinct is what eventually led me to run for office. I never planned to be a politician. But I looked around my community and saw neighbors I care about struggling because of decisions made far away from them. I saw families stressed about healthcare costs, about wages that don't keep up with expenses, about whether they could give their kids the life they dream of. I saw people working hard and still feeling like they were falling behind. And I couldn't stop thinking: we can do better than this. I'm ready to be that change as a representative who listens first. I won't be scared to challenge what isn't working and work together toward real solutions. = Thank you, Christina Christina Bohannan is a mom, law professor, engineer and former state representative. body:
The resources we raise right now allow us to get ads on the air and make sure voters know about our off-season election.
# [](https://act.chrisforjustice.com/go/18?refcode=em20260120-1035&t=1&akid=1036%2E294397%2E1YQjh7)
Most campaigns have 10+ months to build toward Election Day in November.
Ours doesn’t.
**Our Wisconsin Supreme Court election is in April,_not_ November.** That means we have less than three months to:
* Reach voters across the state
* Introduce them to Judge Chris Taylor
* Explain what’s at stake for our courts, our freedoms, and our democracy
* Build the organizing and turnout operation needed to win

And we have to do all of that _before_ most voters are even tuned in to politics.
**That’s why early money matters so much in this race.**

subject: “Because of your accent”
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ILHAN FOR CONGRESS
body:
This is a new low for civil rights and American freedom.
# [](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/35?t=1&akid=2034%2E791427%2EhoNu5P)
[](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/4802?t=2&akid=2034%2E791427%2EhoNu5P)
Friend, we knew that ICE has been racially profiling Latino, Somali-American, and Asian-American people in Minnesota.
But this is a new low for civil rights and American freedom.
In the video above, an ICE agent stops a man in Minneapolis and says to him: “Talking to you, hearing that you have an accent, I have reason to believe that you are not born of this country” and demands that the man now prove his citizenship on the spot.
The man with an “accent” is a US citizen, and has been for years. ICE detained him in front of his five-year-old child anyway, because their policy is to arrest first, check documents later.
Friend, here’s the beginning text of the Fourth Amendment of the US Constitution:
“The right of the people to be secure in their persons, houses, papers, and effects, against unreasonable searches and seizures, shall not be violated...”
Where you were born, what accent you have, the color of your skin; these are all things that are completely off limits for any other law enforcement to use as a basis for search and seizure. But ICE gets away with outright racial profiling and a suspension of civil rights, because MAGA-control in Washington has enabled them to throw out the rule of law and replace it with Trump’s agenda.
**The fight against ICE is the civil rights struggle of our time.** This isn’t about immigrants vs. citizens. This isn’t about criminals vs. the innocent. We are watching, in real-time, as ICE degrades the very values that form the bedrock of our country, and nobody is safe from their terror and brutality.
[**If you are ready to fight back against this insanity, against this complete violation of everything America claims to stand for, chip in to Ilhan Omar’s campaign today. We are building a movement to oppose this ICE occupation, both in Minneapolis and in Congress, and defeat the far-right politicians who have put the Constitution through the shredder.**](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-jan26.B2OwkJ&refcode=em260120-1-180&t=3&akid=2034%2E791427%2EhoNu5P)

Peter , Yesterday, on MLK Day, our team marched with neighbors across this district, and I kept thinking about a Dr. King quote that we need to hold close these days: _" The arc of the moral universe is long, but it bends toward justice."_ But the key to that quote that a lot of people forget is this arc does not bend on its own. name: LeftNet
subject: One year since Trump returned to the White House
body:
Let’s make 2026 the year we start picking up the pieces and putting our country back together.
#
**Today marks one year since Donald Trump returned to the White House, and it’s hard to overstate how much damage has been done.**
In just the last year, we’ve watched:
* Working people fall behind as job growth and wage gains have gone down.
* Tariffs drive up prices on everyday goods instead of making life more affordable.
* Dangerous, unchecked militarism, with strikes and threats on Venezuela and Yemen, carried out without congressional approval.
* ICE raids and abuse escalate, marked by violence, illegal arrests, and families ripped apart, with absolutely no oversight and far too much impunity.

The list could go on and on.
But at LeftNet, we believe we are not powerless. **Real change won’t come from doomscrolling or waiting for someone else to fix it. It’ll come from people who will show up consistently and meaningfully.** That means voting in every election this year, talking with friends and neighbors about what’s happening and what we can do to stop it, and helping people get registered and make a plan to vote.
If you’re angry, you’re not alone. If you’re tired, you’re not alone.
Let’s turn that energy into action and make 2026 the year we start picking up the pieces and putting our country back together.
In solidarity,
LeftNet

**LeftNet is an online political network fighting for progressive causes and candidates focused on social, racial, economic, and environmental justice.**

Peter,
The South is rising again.
Trump has ordered the National Parks Service to remove any mention of slavery from our National Parks, he's attacked the Smithsonian for focusing too much on "how bad slavery was," and he is restoring the names of military bases formerly named after Confederate generals.
MAGA's white supremacist and neo-Confederate lobbies are triumphant and on the march and now Trump is about to throw them their biggest bone yet: the erasure of every Black Congressional district in the South.

Trump's Supreme Court is potentially months to weeks away from ruling to strike down a key portion of the 1965 Voting Rights Act which guarantees congressional representation for African Americans and minorities.
The evisceration of this legislation, which helped end Jim Crow, brings us one step closer to the ethnostate that MAGA's white supremacists hope to realize. GOP legislatures will soon be able to redistrict these formerly Black seats and apportion them out to GOP good 'ol boys.
If and when SCOTUS guts this critical legislation MAGA will take as many as 25 House Seats from Democrats. Enough seats to create a near bulletproof GOP House majority and enshrine one party rule. Checkmate.
MAGA is moving fast. Our only recourse is redistricting blue states to counteract the seats MAGA is stealing. The brave people of California and Virginia were the first to do it, more must follow if we hope to survive the rest of the Trump administration.
Blue state Colorado is the next in line with Colorado Draws the Line spearheading the effort to get new maps on the ballot that will erase 3 MAGA districts (including Boebert's seat) and turn them deep blue.
The time for Democrats to prepare our counter is now. If we wait until the SCOTUS ruling it will be too late. [Please can you rush a donation of what you are able to? **HB145:** This bill raises multiple sales and excise tax rates on firearms, ammunition, archery equipment, certain recreational vehicles, alcohol, cigarettes and other tobacco/vapor products and dedicates the new revenue to a permanent state fund subsidizing hospitals' uncompensated care.
### **Full Analysis**
#### **Vote Statement**
_A vote against this bill is a vote to reject multiple targeted tax hikes on consumers and gun owners and to oppose a new permanent hospital subsidy funded by higher consumption taxes._
#### **Key Provisions & Tradeoffs**
* Raises the sales tax rate from the general 7% to 8% on firearms, ammunition, archery equipment, motorcycles, ATVs and jet skis starting July 1, 2026.
* Increases the retail sales tax rate on alcoholic beverages from 7% to 8%.
* Broadens and increases excise taxes on cigarettes, other tobacco, and newly defined vapor products, and dedicates all incremental tax revenue to a new Mississippi Hospitals Uncompensated Care Assistance Fund in the state treasury.

#### **Liberty Analysis**
Viewed through a limited‐government, free‐market lens, HB145 is primarily a multi‐pronged tax‐increase and spending‐earmark bill. It raises consumption taxes on several categories of goods--firearms and ammunition, archery equipment, motorcycles, ATVs, jet skis, alcohol, and tobacco/vapor products--and dedicates the incremental revenue to a new state‐run hospital uncompensated care fund. That combination directly conflicts with a preference for lower, simpler, broad‐based taxes and smaller, less centralized state spending. Rather than broad tax relief or structural health‐care reform, it uses selective tax penalties to expand a permanent subsidy stream for hospitals.

Economically, the bill increases the overall tax burden on consumers, including many middle‐ and working‐class residents who purchase these legal products. Excise and targeted sales taxes are among the most distortionary and regressive types of taxation. They pick winners and losers in the marketplace and encourage more political engineering of what citizens "should" or "shouldn't" buy. The creation of the Mississippi Hospitals Uncompensated Care Assistance Fund, administered by the Department of Health, shifts more health‐care financing into a tax‐funded government channel. That entrenches dependence on ongoing state revenue, rather than incentivizing competitive pricing, charity care, direct‐care models, or private insurance solutions. From a sound‐money and fiscal‐responsibility perspective, dedicated revenue streams for specific spending constituencies are politically hard to unwind and contribute to long‐run government growth.

From a civil‐liberties and property‐rights standpoint, the bill does not overtly adjust due process, surveillance, or policing powers. However, specifically increasing taxes on firearms, ammunition and archery equipment does amount to a financial penalty on the exercise of a core constitutional right and normal sporting activities. Using the tax code to discourage lawful gun ownership is inconsistent with both limited government and respect for individual rights. More broadly, the bill reinforces a pattern where perceived social or health problems trigger new government revenue schemes instead of deregulation and decentralization. The cumulative effect is more centralized control of resources, more reliance on state‐managed transfer programs, and less space for voluntary, market‐based solutions in health care and consumer choice.

Key Provisions & Tradeoffs Raises the sales tax rate from the general 7% to 8% on firearms, ammunition, archery equipment, motorcycles, ATVs and jet skis starting July 1, 2026. Increases the retail sales tax rate on alcoholic beverages from 7% to 8%. Broadens and increases excise taxes on cigarettes, other tobacco, and newly defined vapor products, and dedicates all incremental tax revenue to a new Mississippi Hospitals Uncompensated Care Assistance Fund in the state treasury. Liberty Analysis Viewed through a limited‐government, free‐market lens, HB145 is primarily a multi‐pronged tax‐increase and spending‐earmark bill. It raises consumption taxes on several categories of goods--firearms and ammunition, archery equipment, motorcycles, ATVs, jet skis, alcohol, and tobacco/vapor products--and dedicates the incremental revenue to a new state‐run hospital uncompensated care fund. That combination directly conflicts with a preference for lower, simpler, broad‐based taxes and smaller, less centralized state spending. Rather than broad tax relief or structural health‐care reform, it uses selective tax penalties to expand a permanent subsidy stream for hospitals. Economically, the bill increases the overall tax burden on consumers, including many middle‐ and working‐class residents who purchase these legal products. Excise and targeted sales taxes are among the most distortionary and regressive types of taxation. They pick winners and losers in the marketplace and encourage more political engineering of what citizens "should" or "shouldn't" buy. The creation of the Mississippi Hospitals Uncompensated Care Assistance Fund, administered by the Department of Health, shifts more health‐care financing into a tax‐funded government channel. That entrenches dependence on ongoing state revenue, rather than incentivizing competitive pricing, charity care, direct‐care models, or private insurance solutions. From a sound‐money and fiscal‐responsibility perspective, dedicated revenue streams for specific spending constituencies are politically hard to unwind and contribute to long‐run government growth. From a civil‐liberties and property‐rights standpoint, the bill does not overtly adjust due process, surveillance, or policing powers. However, specifically increasing taxes on firearms, ammunition and archery equipment does amount to a financial penalty on the exercise of a core constitutional right and normal sporting activities. Using the tax code to discourage lawful gun ownership is inconsistent with both limited government and respect for individual rights. More broadly, the bill reinforces a pattern where perceived social or health problems trigger new government revenue schemes instead of deregulation and decentralization. The cumulative effect is more centralized control of resources, more reliance on state‐managed transfer programs, and less space for voluntary, market‐based solutions in health care and consumer choice. name: AOC
subject: I'm used to being underestimated
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
Moving politics in the direction of the working class requires the working class.
#
When I ran in 2018, I had no money. I was outspent 10 to 1. Millions of dollars were spent against me.
And it’s funny, because the political establishment likes to tell this story where they say, “Oh, no one saw her coming! They fell asleep at the wheel!”
That is not true. **They tell that story so they look like they didn’t lose**.
Ironically, the morning after I won, Andrew Cuomo of all people said that my existence was a ‘fluke.' That I was here by accident.
And that’s not surprising. I’m used to being underestimated.
But what people don’t often see and understand is that **you can outwork that**.
A lot of times people think that being engaged is either _electoral_ or it’s all _activism_ — but it’s actually the combined power of _both_ of these things that have prevented autocracies from taking over in other circumstances.
**Because moving politics in the direction of the working class _requires_ the working class.**
Today marks one year since the second Trump administration began.
2026 will be a critical year for our movement. We must rally together to support progressives who are facing off against opponents — from both parties — who are handing the keys to our country over to billionaires and special interests.

In solidarity,
Alexandria

subject: Anyone else alarmed?

body:

It’s been one year since Donald Trump was inaugurated.

Twelve months later, the damage is impossible to ignore.

Trump has attacked our democracy, shredded civil rights, and corrupted the
courts to serve his own agenda.

His first year back in office has been a campaign of destruction:

* Weaponizing the justice system against anyone who refuses to bow to
him — from Letitia James to James Comey to Jerome Powell.
* Rewarding lawbreakers while punishing critics, including pardoning
over 1,500 Jan 6th insurrectionists.
* Attacking civil rights and vulnerable communities, dismantling federal
agencies, and sending the National Guard and ICE into cities over
local leaders’ protests.
* And when the law gets inconvenient? He runs straight to the Supreme
Court, exploiting the shadow docket to override lower court rulings
and dodge accountability whenever it suits him.

Trump’s message couldn’t be clearer: the courts aren’t a safeguard.
They’re a shortcut to expedite his self-serving agenda.

Demand Justice isn’t waiting another three years to clean up Trump’s
wreckage.

We’re fighting now to reform the courts, block Trump’s consolidation of
power, hold him and his allies accountable, and rebuild a justice system
that works for the people — not billionaires, cronies, or would-be
strongmen.

subject: Launching TODAY: We're taking on the oligarchs
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Our Revolution click here to unsubscribe

[ stdin# ]Our Revolution Logo

Peter Willis,

One year ago today, Trump was inaugurated to his second term.

Even though he vowed to fight for working people, Trump has turned OUR
government into a cash machine for oligarchs – privatizing our government
and plundering taxpayer dollars. While families struggle with rising
costs, Trump is funneling public money, political favors, and government
resources into the pockets of his donors, cronies, and his own family
businesses.

And now we have a plan to stop him.

TODAY, on the anniversary of Trump's return to power, Our Revolution is
working with members of Congress, including US Rep. Rashida Tlaib, to
introduce our groundbreaking resolution to end billionaire power over our
politics. And Our Revolution is launching our "Defund the Oligarchy"
campaign to make it happen – but we need you with us.

Congress must act now to stop billionaires and corporate giants from
buying elections, capturing our government, and rigging the economy in
their favor. Because one thing is certain: we can't solve the climate
crisis, win Medicare for All, or protect our rights as long as oligarchs
control the system.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/34947?source=email-20260120&t=1017&akid=10098%2E5885482%2EwQxNH8 ]Add your name now: Tell Congress to support the resolution to Defund
the Oligarchs and Fund the People.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/34947?source=email-20260120&t=1018&akid=10098%2E5885482%2EwQxNH8 ]ADD YOUR NAME

While families struggle to afford rent, groceries, and healthcare,
America's 900 billionaires now own more wealth than the poorest 67 million
U.S. households *combined*. That's not just inequality – it's oligarchy.

We dug into the numbers. In the last election, Trump's mega-donors from
crypto, oil & gas, and deportation industries funneled $700 million into
his campaign and MAGA causes. Their ROI? Over $172.5 billion in tax breaks
and contracts. For every $1 million they spent, they raked in $18 BILLION.
That isn't democracy; it's daylight robbery.

When Trump promised to "drain the swamp," he actually turned the White
House into a gold mine for the ultra-rich. So we're working with our
allies in Congress to finally:

* End pay-to-play corruption and taxpayer giveaways to billionaire
insiders.
* Get big money out of our elections to stop our voices being drowned
out by billionaire spending.
* Break up corporate monopolies in Big Tech, Big Oil, Wall Street, and
corporate media.
* Tax the ultra-rich and corporate giants so we can finally fund
healthcare, housing, education, and climate action for everyone.
* Build real people power: strengthening unions, expanding worker
ownership, and defending democracy from authoritarian threats.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/34947?source=email-20260120&t=1019&akid=10098%2E5885482%2EwQxNH8 ]Graphic with quote from The Guardian: Rashida Tlaib to intro bill
halting subsidies, tax boons for billionaire oligarchs

The resolution is critical, and Our Revolution is demanding every
member of Congress support it so that we can finally Defund the
Oligarchs and Fund the People. But we need EVERYONE with us.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/34947?source=email-20260120&t=1020&akid=10098%2E5885482%2EwQxNH8 ]Tell your member of Congress: Support the resolution to Defund the
Oligarchs and Fund the People.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/34947?source=email-20260120&t=1021&akid=10098%2E5885482%2EwQxNH8 ]ADD YOUR NAME

Public anger is growing and Congress is feeling the heat. But this
resolution will only succeed with a massive outpouring from the
grassroots – people like you, demanding a government that works "for
us, not billionaire donors."

We don't have the luxury of waiting – billionaires are cashing in on
our dime right now. So let's come together to defund the oligarchy
NOW!

When we organize, we win,

Our Revolution

| | Charlie Kirk built a movement for truth -- but his final message pointed to something eternal.

Peter, it’s been
one year since Trump was sworn back into office.

The man lies more than he breathes, but there’s one thing he didn’t lie
about. He said he’d be a dictator on day one. A year later, we’re living
with the consequences of that promise.

From the start, Trump has used his power to settle scores and silence
dissent. He’s gone after anyone who won’t fall in line — targeting
political opponents, attacking news and media outlets, and demanding
loyalty to himself over the Constitution.

He’s excused political violence, rewarded those who tried to overturn an
election, and made it clear that the rules only apply to some — never to
him, MAGA extremists, or his billionaire allies.

He’s ripped away civil rights protections and legitimized discrimination
at the highest levels of government.

He sent federal forces into cities over the objections of local leaders,
dismantled critical federal agencies under the guise of “efficiency,” and
prioritized mass deportations and mass firings that have devastated
families and communities across the country.

This is what authoritarianism looks like,
Peter. And when people stand up to
it, Trump attacks them.

That’s why Alexandria, Ayanna, Ilhan, and Rashida are constant targets of
his lies, racism, xenophobia, and hate. Not because they’re wrong — but
because they’re effective. Because they refuse to be intimidated. Because
they organize alongside the people and speak truth to power, no matter the
cost.

The Squad isn’t here to make peace with authoritarianism. They’re here to
confront it head-on. They’re fighting for a democracy where working people
actually have power, where our rights aren’t negotiable, and where no one
— not even a president — is above the law. But this fight takes all of us.

name: Eliza Walton
subject: Protect clean air & water — fund natural resources agencies
body:
https://forms.gle/MWdhyX53rvKBHREb6 [https://forms.gle/MWdhyX53rvKBHREb6]
Dear Peter,
OLCV is partnering with environmental and climate justice partners to call for full funding of Oregon’s natural resources agencies, and we need your voice there to get it done.
When: Thursday, February 5th from 12-2pm
Where: Oregon State Capitol, Salem
RSVP here [https://forms.gle/MWdhyX53rvKBHREb6]
Wear BLACK!
In order to finance taxpayer handouts to powerful corporations and wealthy investors (included in Trump’s "Big Beautiful Bill"), Oregon lawmakers are considering cuts. And yet again, our natural resources agencies like the Department of Environmental Quality (DEQ) and Department of Land Conservation and Development (DLCD) are on the chopping block. These agencies ensure that Oregonians have clean air and water, healthy oceans, and protected lands, and they are vital to our public health and community well-being. Our transportation and climate programs like heat pumps and electric vehicle rebates, are also on the line. Join us for a rally in Salem on Thursday, February 5th from 12pm-2pm. [https://forms.gle/MWdhyX53rvKBHREb6]
The climate justice, transportation, and conservation communities are coming together with a broad coalition of progressive partners to rally in Salem and show lawmakers that Oregonians are counting on them to fund essential agencies and programs. We will rally in solidarity with labor, education, hunger, immigration, housing, choice advocates, and more. We need YOU to show up big for climate, transportation, conservation, wildlife, clean air and water, and make sure we stand out in the crowd.
More specific details will be shared closer to the event. Please feel free to invite other climate advocates and activists in your networks-- the more the merrier!
In solidarity,
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/AV/AVLCV/1/70877/images/Eliza.png]
Eliza Walton (she/they)

name: True the Vote
subject: Mount Vernon, This Moment, and What Comes Next
body:
Pray. Serve. Vote.
| | | January 20, 2026 | [**Read Online**](https://de717de0.click.convertkit-mail2.com/92u79dlprzbnh640p9ns9hzoxm933bwhn03e8/n2hohvhv2n84ges6/aHR0cHM6Ly9ja2FyY2hpdmUuY29tL2IvcWR1OGg3aDRlenJucWZ6d25ubXc3dTgycHZya2tpNGhrb3Z4OQ==) |
---

Hi Friend —
I wanted to take a moment to share some news with you — both personal and professional.
First, a bit of personal joy. Our family recently welcomed our first grandchild, a grandson, and my heart is full in a way that’s hard to put into words! I’m a grandmother! Moments like this have a way of clarifying everything. They remind me why True the Vote’s work matters — for our children, for their children, and for the country they will one day inherit. We cannot fail.
Second, I’m excited to share that we’ve officially launched True the Vote NOW, our new C4 organization. This step gives us the ability to engage in ways we simply couldn’t before — to move faster, speak more directly, and press harder for accountability and real reform. It opens an important new channel for our work, and I’m grateful to be stepping into it with you.
That expanded capability matters now more than ever.
This week, I’m in Washington, D.C., meeting with allies and building momentum. What’s at stake is real. If liberty loses ground in Congress, hard-won progress will be rolled back almost immediately. That reality is shaping every conversation I’m having here, and it underscores just how urgent this work is as we look toward 2026.
I remember first coming to Washington as an activist in 2009. At the time, I was green — blissfully unaware of the odyssey ahead. I experience this city very differently now. There’s a weight, a darkness. You can sense it almost immediately. But the passion of history’s call is here, too. Yesterday, instead of heading to a meeting or my hotel, I went straight to Mount Vernon — to ground where real patriots walked, to a shared spirit that still lives within us.
_Me at Mount Vernon - January 19, 2026_
---
And so, despite the darkness, I’ve come to build on something that gives me real hope: a small, serious group of people working quietly and deliberately toward real results. No theatrics. No posturing. Just focused, determined work to fix what’s broken.
That same seriousness is guiding us as we prepare for a season of significant growth at True the Vote. Our focus is simple and unapologetic: empowering citizens to secure election integrity locally. We are expanding our efforts to equip activists in their own communities with the tools they need — from registering eligible voters, to reviewing and challenging voter rolls, to being trained, mobilized, and ready to work inside the election process itself. This movement will not be sustained from Washington. It will be secured by informed, equipped citizens at the local level.
There is much work to be done, and this season feels urgent. I feel it deeply.
Thank you for coming on this journey with us. You make this work possible, and I never take that for granted.
God bless you, and God bless America. Keep the faith. Never quit.
Ever onward —
Catherine

clean_body: Pray. Serve. Vote. | | | January 20, 2026 | == | Hi Friend — I wanted to take a moment to share some news with you — both personal and professional. First, a bit of personal joy. Our family recently welcomed our first grandchild, a grandson, and my heart is full in a way that’s hard to put into words! I’m a grandmother! Moments like this have a way of clarifying everything. They remind me why True the Vote’s work matters — for our children, for their children, and for the country they will one day inherit. We cannot fail. Second, I’m excited to share that we’ve officially launched True the Vote NOW, our new C4 organization. This step gives us the ability to engage in ways we simply couldn’t before — to move faster, speak more directly, and press harder for accountability and real reform. It opens an important new channel for our work, and I’m grateful to be stepping into it with you. That expanded capability matters now more than ever. This week, I’m in Washington, D.C., meeting with allies and building momentum. What’s at stake is real. If liberty loses ground in Congress, hard-won progress will be rolled back almost immediately. That reality is shaping every conversation I’m having here, and it underscores just how urgent this work is as we look toward 2026. I remember first coming to Washington as an activist in 2009. At the time, I was green — blissfully unaware of the odyssey ahead. I experience this city very differently now. There’s a weight, a darkness. You can sense it almost immediately. But the passion of history’s call is here, too. Yesterday, instead of heading to a meeting or my hotel, I went straight to Mount Vernon — to ground where real patriots walked, to a shared spirit that still lives within us. Me at Mount Vernon - January 19, 2026 And so, despite the darkness, I’ve come to build on something that gives me real hope: a small, serious group of people working quietly and deliberately toward real results. No theatrics. No posturing. Just focused, determined work to fix what’s broken. That same seriousness is guiding us as we prepare for a season of significant growth at True the Vote. Our focus is simple and unapologetic: empowering citizens to secure election integrity locally. We are expanding our efforts to equip activists in their own communities with the tools they need — from registering eligible voters, to reviewing and challenging voter rolls, to being trained, mobilized, and ready to work inside the election process itself. This movement will not be sustained from Washington. It will be secured by informed, equipped citizens at the local level. There is much work to be done, and this season feels urgent. I feel it deeply. Thank you for coming on this journey with us. You make this work possible, and I never take that for granted. God bless you, and God bless America. Keep the faith. Never quit. Ever onward — Catherine | | | == | Update your or unsubscribe © 2025 True the Vote 3120 Southwest Frwy Ste 101, PMB 19128, Houston, Texas 77098-4520

name: John Bisognano, Redistricting Action
subject: Here’s why we have a new name:
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY THE NATIONAL REDISTRICTING ACTION FUND
body:
We are as committed as ever to ensuring a democracy where every voter counts.
|
---

Peter,
We’ve gotten a few questions about why we have officially changed our organization’s name to **Redistricting Action.**
Here’s what I say: Our new name reflects both who we are and what this moment demands.
Redistricting is no longer a once-every-decade process — it’s an ongoing struggle for a representative democracy. **And we are here to take action. To organize. To make sure every map, in every state, truly represents the people.**
These are existential times for our democracy. In the days ahead, as many as seven states could start the process of redrawing their congressional maps. And while the nation’s redistricting crisis is already expanding, we’re awaiting a Supreme Court ruling that could weaken the Voting Rights Act and give cover to several other states to manipulate their own maps and take power away from communities of color.
We are building Redistricting Action to meet this moment by providing grassroots activists with all of the information, tools, and opportunities needed to defend our democracy.
[**With your generosity, we can strengthen these efforts on the front lines of present and future attacks — and ensure that our democracy emerges from this crisis stronger, fairer, and firmly in the hands of the American people.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/123702429/596280753/742152064?refcode=don_aotl_tier1_email_NewName_email_20260120-AOTL-Tier1-NewName_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20260120-AOTL-Tier1-NewName_&utm_campaign=NewName&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk2IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImM3MGZmNmYzLTQ5ZjYtZjAxMS04ZDRjLTAwMjI0ODJkMjc5YiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=qUkig0dGex56JegDAoxhjuyoTUXEzj5tS1q5559XZv8=)
Our long-term vision remains the same: The United States needs national redistricting standards that require all states to follow the same rules, ensuring fair, independently drawn maps and a political system that reflects the will of the people.
Because redistricting has become weaponized by power-hungry politicians who want to skirt accountability, we are empowering activists right now to take on this very challenge.
[**Make a grassroots donation today to help deliver high-quality training, step-by-step information, and more support for people who are fighting gerrymandering across the country.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/123702430/596280755/742152064?refcode=don_aotl_tier1_email_NewName_email_20260120-AOTL-Tier1-NewName_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20260120-AOTL-Tier1-NewName_&utm_campaign=NewName&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk2IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImM3MGZmNmYzLTQ5ZjYtZjAxMS04ZDRjLTAwMjI0ODJkMjc5YiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=qUkig0dGex56JegDAoxhjuyoTUXEzj5tS1q5559XZv8=)
You and I know that our work isn’t easy, but when we’ve invested in our mission and when we’ve organized where it matters most, we’ve won. Our collective action to defend fair maps for all is powerful — and right now, it’s more important than ever to keep up this critical work.
Thank you for moving our democracy forward,
— Biz
John Bisognano
President
Redistricting Action

My story. Our fight.
# [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/123702434/596280762/938567526?refcode=header&noskip=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MTcxOSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2ZTBkYzYxNi00YWY2LWYwMTEtOGQ0Yy0wMDIyNDgyZDI3OWIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=b9mrlipqIk9kEKpfznkD56YII7jlrOI8xZcs-hWY4RQ=)
As a proud and patriotic immigrant, I want every kid to have the same shot I had — the shot that allowed me to give back to this country.
**[But today, millions of kids and families are being denied that same chance. So I’m asking you to stand with me — and if you can, make a donation today to help me fight for real, comprehensive immigration reform.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/123702435/596280763/789508428?refcode=2601120_RG_sameshot&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MTcxOSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2ZTBkYzYxNi00YWY2LWYwMTEtOGQ0Yy0wMDIyNDgyZDI3OWIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=b9mrlipqIk9kEKpfznkD56YII7jlrOI8xZcs-hWY4RQ=)**
[DONATE NOW](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/123702436/596280764/-309737922?refcode=2601120_RG_sameshot&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MTcxOSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2ZTBkYzYxNi00YWY2LWYwMTEtOGQ0Yy0wMDIyNDgyZDI3OWIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=b9mrlipqIk9kEKpfznkD56YII7jlrOI8xZcs-hWY4RQ=)
My mom brought me to this country not knowing English and without an education. But thanks to a progressive immigration law passed by Congress in the 1980s, we were able to apply for permanent legal residency. I became a U.S. citizen in my early 20s.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/123702437/596280765/-1909961190?refcode=2601120_RG_sameshot&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MTcxOSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2ZTBkYzYxNi00YWY2LWYwMTEtOGQ0Yy0wMDIyNDgyZDI3OWIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=b9mrlipqIk9kEKpfznkD56YII7jlrOI8xZcs-hWY4RQ=&emci=660dc616-4af6-f011-8d4c-0022482d279b&emdi=6e0dc616-4af6-f011-8d4c-0022482d279b&ceid=16877361)
_**That act of Congress changed everything. **_
America gave me the opportunity to go to school, to serve my community, and to become the first LGBTQ immigrant ever elected to Congress. **I know my story isn’t typical, but it should be. I believe every family should have access to that same pathway to success.**
Right now, Congress should be an institution that helps people — not one that blocks progress or plays politics with families’ futures. But we’re facing big, structural challenges:
* Generational poverty
* Concentrated wealth and power
* Attacks on democracy
* Systemic racism
* And a fringe minority inside the GOP is determined to stop any meaningful immigration reform

I’ve seen firsthand that coalitions can be built — even when the opposition is entrenched, ideological, and loud. We can do big things when we insist on justice and fight for opportunity.
**[That’s why I need you with me. Congress cannot keep punting on this. Families cannot wait. Kids cannot wait. Please chip in right now to help power this fight for immigration reform.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/123702438/596280766/789508428?refcode=2601120_RG_sameshot&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MTcxOSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2ZTBkYzYxNi00YWY2LWYwMTEtOGQ0Yy0wMDIyNDgyZDI3OWIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=b9mrlipqIk9kEKpfznkD56YII7jlrOI8xZcs-hWY4RQ=)**
[DONATE NOW](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/123702439/596280767/-309737922?refcode=2601120_RG_sameshot&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MTcxOSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2ZTBkYzYxNi00YWY2LWYwMTEtOGQ0Yy0wMDIyNDgyZDI3OWIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=b9mrlipqIk9kEKpfznkD56YII7jlrOI8xZcs-hWY4RQ=)
Thank you for believing in a more compassionate, inclusive, and hopeful America.
Robert Garcia

**KTR: One Year In, Trump Is Delivering Results** _Promises Made. Promises Kept._
**PHOENIX** — Karrin Taylor Robson, conservative business executive and Trump-endorsed candidate for governor of Arizona, released the following statement today marking the one-year anniversary of President Trump’s second inauguration:
_One year ago today, I was in Washington for President Trump’s second inauguration. He took office with a clear mandate from the American people to close the border and hold Washington accountable._
_One year into his term, President Trump is carrying out the America First Agenda that Americans overwhelmingly voter for. He shut down the border and is removing the most violent criminals from our country. He put America First again by confronting hostile regimes and reasserting U.S. leadership on the world stage. He unleashed American energy, cut red tape, and delivered the largest tax cut ever. He has put working families and small businesses ahead of career politicians in Washington._
_Most importantly, President Trump has proved once again that conservative leadership works. Costs are coming down, jobs are coming back, and Americans finally have a president who fights for them instead of apologizing for them._
_Arizona continues to feel the consequences of Joe Biden and Katie Hobbs’ failures firsthand. That is why President Trump’s leadership matters so much to our state. We need leaders at every level who will work with him, not against him._
_As governor, I will stand with President Trump to keep our border secure, crush the cartels, cut taxes, rein in waste and abuse and make Arizona strong, safe and affordable again._
_President Trump has proved in just one year what happens when you put a results-driven leader, not another career politician, in charge. America is coming back, and Arizona will, too._
---
| |
**About Karrin Taylor Robson** Karrin Taylor Robson is a lifelong conservative and business executive running for Governor of Arizona with President Trump’s endorsement.
Just like President Trump, Karrin is not a politician; she is a self-made business executive who has built one of the state’s leading land-use and economic development firms. Her work has helped bring jobs, opportunity, and growth to Arizona while cutting through bureaucracy and fighting government overreach. She’s also served on key military and education boards that impact Arizona families every day, including for more than 20 years on the Air Force Chief of Staff’s Civic Leaders Group.
A proud wife, mother, and grandmother, Karrin is running for Governor to keep our communities safe, fix, root out waste, fraud, and abuse in Arizona, and she will always have President Trump's back.

body:
# [](https://act.angela4congress.com/go/60?refcode=em20260120-229&t=1&akid=229%2E66908%2EcDP6Hx)
Angela Gonzales-Torres is a pro-human rights candidate running to represent CA-34. Email is one of the most important ways that we can keep you informed on this critical race, but if you want to stop receiving emails from us, [**click here**](https://act.angela4congress.com/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?t=2&akid=229%2E66908%2EcDP6Hx).
---
[](https://act.angela4congress.com/go/128?c0=em_ms_agt_welcome_2._EQA7o&amount=5&refcode=em20260120-229&t=3&akid=229%2E66908%2EcDP6Hx)
_“Angela is exactly what Los Angeles needs in Congress right now: a working-class champion with the moral courage to not only fight back against the Trump administration’s cruelty with the urgency it demands but also take on the Democratic Party when the corporate establishment fails to fight for our communities.”_
Hey, it’s Alexandra Rojas! I’m the Executive Director of Justice Democrats and I’m coming to you personally today to explain why Justice Democrats endorsed Angela for Congress.
I said it to Politico, and I’ll say it again: **Angela is exactly what Los Angeles needs in Congress right now.**
Angela is a 30-year-old, working-class champion with a strong moral backbone and a steadfast commitment to her community. Unlike CA-34’s current Representative, she will not only fight back against the Trump administration’s chaos and cruelty with the urgency it demands, but also take on the Democratic Party when the corporate establishment fails to fight for our communities.
And like all Justice Democrats, Angela isn’t taking a dime of corporate PAC money: unlike Jimmy Gomez, she won’t be answering to Trump’s donors or real estate developers. Her campaign is a people-powered community movement — and that’s one of many reasons why we are so proud to support her.
[**Will you help us set Angela up for success by pitching in any amount now? It’s still early in this race, and every single donation makes a huge difference.**](https://act.angela4congress.com/go/128?c0=em_ms_agt_welcome_2._EQA7o&amount=5&refcode=em20260120-229&t=4&akid=229%2E66908%2EcDP6Hx)
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.angela4congress.com/go/128?c0=em_ms_agt_welcome_2._EQA7o&amount=5&refcode=em20260120-229&t=23&akid=229%2E66908%2EcDP6Hx)**
Angela is a born-and-raised Angeleno who understands her community’s most pressing issues because she’s lived them. **Growing up in East LA as the daughter of a deportee and a single mother, she experienced the terrifying reality of family separation firsthand, after her father was deported when Angela was just 15.** Her mother was left to raise Angela and her 3 sisters alone overnight — a nightmare more and more families across Los Angeles, California, and beyond are experiencing themselves as Trump and his ICE goons take over and terrify communities nationwide.
Since 2017, the working-class community Angela grew up in and still lives in today has been represented by **Rep. Jimmy Gomez** , a politician who’d like you to think he’s a progressive, but who, in reality, has made his career doing AIPAC’s bidding, voting to pass Trump’s crypto agenda, and selling out to industries like private equity and real estate.
Gomez’s campaign relies on the same lobbies that fuel Trump’s rise, destabilize our economy, and displace our neighbors.
But where Gomez went to Washington D.C. and closed the door on his constituents, Angela is rooted in her lifelong community. From seeing her neighbors, teachers, and classmates come together to support her family after her father’s deportation, to watching her mom work two and three jobs to make ends meet, to serving as the President of her local elected Neighborhood Council, Angela’s experiences are the foundation of her values, advocacy, and unwavering commitment to fight for working families like her own.
This race is about a young, working-class Angeleno running to represent the working-class community she was born and raised in, versus a corporate member of the political establishment who has turned his back on that very community for some PAC checks.
Angela can take Jimmy on and win, but it’s going to take a groundswell of grassroots support from this progressive movement. This race isn’t just about Los Angeles — it’s about whether our Congress will be powered by working-class fighters like Angela, or bought off by corporate PACs and Trump’s billionaire backers like Jimmy Gomez.
[**Help Justice Democrats send Angela to Congress and send a message loud and clear to all of CA-34 and beyond: East LA won’t be bought. Donate anything you can today to help make a difference.**](https://act.angela4congress.com/go/128?c0=em_ms_agt_welcome_2._EQA7o&amount=5&refcode=em20260120-229&t=24&akid=229%2E66908%2EcDP6Hx)
Thanks for your support,
Alexandra Rojas
Executive Director
Justice Democrats

**[Donate](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_agt_footer?refcode=em20260120-229-&t=25&refcode2=229_66908_cDP6Hx&akid=229%2E66908%2EcDP6Hx)**

Every day seems to bring us some new Trump/MAGA horror related to our fundamental rights. Now, more than ever since Dr. King's time, it shows us how important this movement to protect our right to vote and our access to things like early voting, drop boxes, and mail-in ballots truly is.
Fuel our efforts to defend voting rights and make every voice heard in our elections across the country with $35 or more right now >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=012026_2&amount=35]
https://voteractionproject.org/ [https://voteractionproject.org/]
Team,
We are spending today honoring the Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. for the 40th time in our nation's history.
We're also celebrating his legacy at the very moment when the Voting Rights Act, the seminal achievement of the Civil Rights Movement, is on the chopping block at a Supreme Court dominated by MAGA.
The fight for equal access to the ballot and our fundamental right to vote was at the core of Dr. King's mission. In his own words:
“Give us the ballot, and we will no longer have to worry the federal government about our basic rights... Give us the ballot, and we will transform the salient misdeeds of bloodthirsty mobs into the calculated good deeds of orderly citizens.”
You're going to hear a lot of opponents of voting rights mouthing platitudes today. Then you'll hear them wrongly insist the 14th and 15th Amendments prohibit Congress from taking race into account to remedy past discrimination.
MAGA is actively bastardizing our history, their judges ignoring the original meaning of the post-Civil War Amendments and overriding 60 years of precedent, and as a movement, they are destroying Dr. King’s most important achievement.
Our fight is the same as Dr. King's, because the work is never done. Please chip in $35 or whatever you can today to help us protect voting rights nationwide >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=012026_2&amount=35]

That "us" wasn't just the 60's Civil Rights Movement. That "us" isn't just our elected officials, or former presidents, or organizations like ours. That "us" means everyone, every citizen of our country, standing up for our fundamental rights.
There are countless comparisons to be made between the actions of MAGA and President Trump now and the oppression of our past. The very same oppression Dr. King fought has remade itself into a modern movement that's deploying armed federal agents into our cities and threatening our access to the ballot and methods of voting.
Just like Dr. King, we refuse to stand idly by. Help us fight back with $35 or whatever you can to defend the use of vote-by-mail, increase voter participation, and make every vote count in November and beyond >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=012026_2&amount=35]

It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.

Peter, Who actually wants to live in “show me your papers” America? ICE agents are stopping people for walking in their own neighborhoods, pumping gas in their car, or shopping in a grocery store, and demanding that they prove their citizenship. One of the groups ICE is targeting today are Somali Americans in Minneapolis, 87% of whom are U.S. citizens and 60% of whom were born in the United States. ICE’s rampage through Minneapolis is not about deporting undocumented immigrants, they are trying to collectively punish and terrorize people. Peter, we look back in shame at every era in history when these kinds of draconian, authoritarian measures were used to target entire communities. People always ask themselves the same question later: If I had been alive then, would I have tried to stop it? Would I have fought back? This is that moment. This is a deliberate attempt to stop people all across the country from getting information about what is happening in their communities and in their government.

I know I've reached out this week about this issue.My team tells me they've texted and emailed at least twice too!

Especially when our kids are paying attention.

| | | | |
---
Hi Peter, I’ve been thinking a lot lately about what our kids are learning from politics right now. They see the tone leaders use. They see when division gets rewarded. And they see when winning seems to matter more than how you treat people along the way. [****](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/Q3ittgaEnOZHWucfNpvGDg~~/AAUS1hA~/jF6ojVFzBohOPBYirY6Zpph5qe1Acid_bjj4E89LulFCj1R2T07AF6WyN0RuPvuD3SkFYJ-CoUs8UwTIeg1LF8bPPlG5XLhktyHhNEx4ae0RM9bbDfOAQMwCHVICS1XQtYIEfLTlY1Q3VSyxBqeJj2kvKFx4V0sO1czH57cMaFU~) As mayor, I’ve tried to lead with one simple reminder in mind: our kids are watching. Before I speak or make a decision, I ask myself whether it’s something my kids would be proud of. That’s pushed me to lead in a steady, respectful, and focused way, bringing people together rather than pitting neighbors against each other. That approach has mattered because a mayor doesn’t get to represent just one group of people. You represent everyone. Democrats, Republicans, and folks who don’t fit neatly into either category. You listen, you work across differences, and you focus on what actually moves the community forward. We’re building something that rejects constant outrage and still competes seriously. A campaign that proves you can stand for your values, respect people you disagree with, and still win. [**I hope you’ll consider making a contribution today to help us keep building that kind of campaign across TN-05.**](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/T3XIiWUld_CgC_D8cKNZyA~~/AAUS1hA~/MibSnmE3566m9mD8hA_qmuXS8JjwxO5jtfgw4R4cJ6LfCtJcmThF8mzl5E9qFgS9awuSePhWImWVoKieRQ9s3pb-cJ4SWzKmZdt2CNMct4atVYP2dj_taEkZmjRtPZ5mTT-kMh9WHumONm6xHli6IMYFTteNaw0iMSltxRQwdlc~) | | [DONATE](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/GeiY-LKhUlkr092_IZoZAQ~~/AAUS1hA~/MibSnmE3566m9mD8hA_qmuXS8JjwxO5jtfgw4R4cJ6LfCtJcmThF8mzl5E9qFgS9awuSePhWImWVoKieRQ9s3me2F08hpkc0JvWxGCtmrDLLMj-Zz21amm6U-mojVsVvjy-SsbGHp3eqFMBW_5gC2M7K4auF4Z6t6WBFrfz81is~)

Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Peter, For more than two decades, American Veterans Center has been dedicated to honoring the sacrifice and preserving the legacy of our nation's heroes. Each year, we host the **National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C.** , bringing Americans together in a powerful display of remembrance and patriotism. We also proudly produce **" American Valor: A Salute to Our Heroes,"** a nationally televised tribute to the men and women who have served across generations.

But our work goes far beyond public events. At the heart of our mission is a commitment to **preserve the stories of veterans from every era of service** -- from the final voices of World War II, to those who served in Korea, Vietnam, and the post-9/11 generation. Through these efforts, we ensure that future generations understand the cost of freedom and the courage it has taken to defend it.

This year, American Veterans Center is marking historic military milestones: the 250th anniversaries of the U.S. Army, Navy, and Marine Corps...the 80th anniversary of the victories that won World War II...and key events in the Korean War 75 years ago, and the Vietnam War which ended 50 years ago this year.

ICE is no longer a distant threat – they’re here in St. Louis.
ICE agents are showing up in our communities, terrorizing elementary schools, and posted up in places where families should feel safe. Parents are terrified. Kids are scared. Neighbors are being forced to look over their shoulders just to get through the day.
ICE has always been a rogue agency. But under Trump, their budget has ballooned. They’ve come into our communities, targeting our neighbors, and trying to create chaos. They want us to be scared. They want us to be hopeless. They want us to fear them.
And since Renee Nicole Good’s senseless murder, the Trump administration has closed ranks around their ICE brigade, calling her a “domestic terrorist” and spreading blatant misinformation.
Cori has been clear on this since the first day she ran for office: we must abolish ICE. She has St. Louis’ back.
But Cori’s opponent, on the other hand, voted with Republicans just last year to express “gratitude” for ICE and encourage local law enforcement to help them in their mass deportation agenda.
We need a member of Congress who will fight back, and we know that we can have that with Cori.

Hey, Peter, Team Ossoff here. **[Before you click away: we’re asking if you can donate $5 to Jon Ossoff’s reelection campaign today.**](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-jan26.wPRyEn&refcode=em260120-2-f-a&t=1&akid=1476%2E5691347%2EjgLL6g)
Here’s why:
* Jon is MAGA’s #1 target in the midterms, and his reelection will be the toughest in the country.

* Polling shows this race will be _incredibly close,_ and the GOP is already pouring millions of dollars into Georgia to try to overwhelm and drown out our campaign.

* Every single donation not only helps us fight back against these attacks and set the record straight, it’s also a powerful message to Trump, our opponents, and the entire Republican Party that Jon has a MASSIVE grassroots movement behind him.

name: Adam Schiff
subject: What we’ve learned in the first year of Trump 2.0
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY SCHIFF FOR SENATE
body:
|
# [](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/61?t=1&akid=9436%2E5257348%2EnTxLh9)
We’re at an inflection point, Derek. Since Donald Trump was inaugurated for the second time, one year ago today, we have seen irreparable damage done.
From the literal destruction of the East Wing of the White House to tearing down our economy, international standing, and Constitution, this administration has inflicted far more _lasting_ damage than we could have even imagined in just 12 months. He’s thrown every norm of governance out the window and seems intent on creating a permanent MAGA authoritarian regime.
He’s sent armed, masked thugs into our cities to terrorize our communities. He’s turned the independent Justice Department into his private army of lawyers to exact revenge on his political opposition — including me.
He is going after six other Democratic lawmakers for saying that troops are obligated to refuse illegal orders and must abide by the Constitution. He’s now suggested we shouldn’t even have midterms.
He’s making sweeping cuts in funds appropriated by Congress for any program he doesn’t like. He’s decimated the civil service and created chaos at all levels of our federal government.
He has withheld food, housing, and health care assistance for people in need – just because they live in Blue states. His tariffs have added a huge burden to consumers already facing an affordability crisis. His administration has been downright hostile to any attempts to protect our environment, making it as easy as possible for polluters, fossil fuel companies, and toxic waste dumpers to make our air dirtier and water less clean.
**_This is not even remotely a complete list. Not by a long shot._**
All of this has happened with the acquiescence of a Republican Congress and captured courts, which have abdicated their constitutional imperative to provide a check on executive authority.
**But this year has also brought back our ability to resist, to fight back, to come together to hold him and his MAGA counterparts accountable.**
Americans are showing up in huge numbers to protect their neighbors, to resist this takeover of our country. And they showed up at the ballot box in 2025 in elections from Virginia to Georgia, New Jersey, and California to reject Republicans. **We can take our country back this year by flipping the House and Senate.**
_That will take strong leadership. I've put myself on top of the president’s enemies list in the service of our democracy, and I’m proud to be there._
[**I will never stop seeking the truth and pursuing accountability for this corrupt administration. If you’re with me, pitch in today.**](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/1014?c0=q12026_abs_em.43HrbP&refcode=AU_ABS_FR_GEN_GEN_AC90_20260120_PM1_V1_S1&t=4&akid=9436%2E5257348%2EnTxLh9)

name: Eileen for Colorado
subject: Lauren Boebert is failing to defend children in Colorado who are losing access to the critical services that keep them alive.
body:
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | [|
---](https://mailchi.mp/4aa126c541c9/lauren-boebert-voted-no-on-investing-in-farmers-ranchers-and-rural-communities-15534263?e=1c5f08419c)
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | On January 6, **the Department of Health and Human Services announced that they plan to freeze access to federal child care and family assistance funding for five states — including Colorado.**
This announcement **targets services that Colorado families rely on to survive,** and would result in the loss of more than $2 billion from Child Care and Development Fund (CCDF), $7 billion from Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF), and $1 billion from Social Services Block Grant.
**These services have long provided essential relief** for families who rely on childcare access in order to feed and provide for their children. **Services now in jeopardy include access to stable housing, affordable healthcare, food support, and childcare.** Freezing this funding pulls the rug out from under families as they try to make ends meet.
This**targeted, political attack against Colorado** would result in...
* ❌ The **loss of child care** for thousands of Coloradans.
*
❌** Thousands of Colorado kids and families going hungry.**

---
|
---
| | **Eileen wants to make one thing very clear: protecting children should never be a political issue.**
Although Washington is using families and their children as collateral damage in a political game, Eileen refuses to play. She knows that Coloradans have**** no interest in petty political squabbles when their safety and security are being threatened.
**As your congressperson, Eileen promises to...**
* **🥊 Stand up to Washington elites who prioritize partisan goals** over protecting American families.
* * 🏡 Protect federal services that **provide security for Colorado families and children.**
* * **🛒 Crack down on price-gouging** so that critical goods like **groceries are affordable** to every Colorado family.
*

* **❤️🩹 Fight to make healthcare accessible and affordable.**

---
|
---
| | Eileen understands that what matters most right now is the affordability crisis impacting our community. She has traveled across our district— meeting parents and listening to their concerns— and one thing is clear: **Low-income families do not deserve to be punished because of partisan arguments between career politicians.**
**Coloradans are entitled to a representative who is willing to put politics aside to defend our children and keep them safe,** housed, fed, and well-cared for**.** Eileen is prepared to take on this responsibility**.** As a mother, she recognizes the pressure parents face to balance work, family, and rising costs of living. **Governmental failures should never add additional burdens to parents as they navigate raising the next generation.**

---
| | | | | | | | | | | | [**Join Eileen**](https://eileenforcolorado.us12.list-manage.com/track/click?u=400e8fa21dba23169b817268c&id=be554d0499&e=1c5f08419c)**in the fight to protect our families and provide for our children.**
---
| |
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | **About our “What’s at Stake” Series** This newsletter focuses on what is on the line for Colorado if Lauren Boebert remains in Congress. Each edition highlights a real issue facing families in our district, what is driving the problem, and how leadership in Washington can make a tangible difference. From rising health care costs to threats to rural hospitals to the economic pressures on working families, the stakes in this election are real.
**We encourage you to share** these newsletters with friends, neighbors, and on social media so our community can have informed, honest conversations about what this election means for the future of Colorado’s Fourth District

Fellow Patriot, For more than two decades, American Veterans Center has been dedicated to honoring the sacrifice and preserving the legacy of our nation's heroes. Each year, we host the **National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C.** , bringing Americans together in a powerful display of remembrance and patriotism. We also proudly produce **" American Valor: A Salute to Our Heroes,"** a nationally televised tribute to the men and women who have served across generations.

But our work goes far beyond public events. At the heart of our mission is a commitment to **preserve the stories of veterans from every era of service** -- from the final voices of World War II, to those who served in Korea, Vietnam, and the post-9/11 generation. Through these efforts, we ensure that future generations understand the cost of freedom and the courage it has taken to defend it.

This year, American Veterans Center is marking historic military milestones: the 250th anniversaries of the U.S. Army, Navy, and Marine Corps...the 80th anniversary of the victories that won World War II...and key events in the Korean War 75 years ago, and the Vietnam War which ended 50 years ago this year.

#### _**Cliff 's Note:** I was going to write a similar piece myself--but Dan Perry already did it better, more clearly, and more forcefully than I could, so I asked his permission to republish it here. Everyone needs to see the letter Trump sent to the Prime Minister of Norway, because the reason so many Americans still don't grasp how dangerous and mentally unfit he is, is that legacy corporate media refuses to show the full, unfiltered truth._
#### This article was originally published by Dan Perry on his Substack, [Ask Questions Later](https://substack.com/redirect/6f8cf359-cb9e-47dd-b5ff-8857972af668?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), under the same title "[Time for the Twenty-Fifth](https://substack.com/redirect/25e75f70-d558-40ce-9571-40fae5b694a6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)". Blue Amp Media is republishing it here with permission.
#### _**by Dan Perry**_
Last month around this time, in an article entitled "[Peak Lowlife](https://substack.com/redirect/a3ddf45e-e5ea-4caa-9721-2c463a9586a6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)," I asked whether Trump's demonic reaction to the murder of US cultural icon Rob Reiner and his wife Michelle was finally enough to make Republicans understand that he is not an acceptable leader. To anyone who has succeeded in the natural instinct to try to forget, Trump then seemed to rejoice in the murder because Reiner was a critic. The answer to my question, despite some bad polls, was basically no.
Now I must ask the question again, in the wake of Trump's letter to the prime minister of Norway, Jonas Gahr Store. This letter is so absurd that any half-conscious reader must seriously wonder whether the time has not come for a serious discussion of his removal from office via the 25th Amendment to the US Constitution, which enables the vice president and a majority of the Cabinet to declare that a president is unable to discharge the powers and duties of his office. The process this sets off could transfer authority to the disturbing JD Vance, which is cold comfort indeed -- but this is the bed that we have made.
I realize the atmosphere has become so partisan that many people will just swallow any outrage and assume the criticism is automatic, and that there must be some reason or explanation for whatever it is that has people worked up. What's the big deal, some might ask, about whatever Trump writes to the leader of some distant land that doesn't even have an NFL team? All I can say is that this is a letter whose every sentence could never have been written by any predecessor, and which provides overpowering evidence for invoking the Twenty-Fifth.
