As a person who has practiced journalism since high school in America, I still think words have value, which I know is quaint. And from that perspective, I declare that this petulant, infantile, and threatening letter to a blameless NATO ally, which will be studied by historians with disbelief, is actually worth a line-by-line examination. Trust me on this, please, and let us proceed forthwith.
SENTENCE ONE: _**Considering your Country decided not to give me the Nobel Peace Prize for having stopped 8 Wars PLUS, I no longer feel an obligation to think purely of Peace, although it will always be predominant, but can now think about what is good and proper for the United States of America.**_
* It asserts a false premise: Norway does not "decide" who gets the Nobel Peace Prize, which is awarded by an independent Norwegian committee. And it treats the Nobel Prize as a transactional reward whose non-awarding to him personally should affect geopolitical decisions on the part of the US.
* It makes an unsubstantiated and exaggerated claim ("having stopped 8 Wars PLUS") without evidence or international recognition, implying that restraint and responsibility depend on a personal reward for the president. It suggests a shift away from peace as a principle ("I no longer feel an obligation to think purely of Peace") in mafia-like language in communication with an ally.
* It implies that acting in America's interest is somehow opposed to thinking "purely of Peace," and also directly suggests -- incredibly -- that Trump has until now _not_ been pursuing "what is good and proper for the United States of America" (which, I must admit, he actually has not).
* He capitalizes "Country." It's starting to look like he really does not know.

SENTENCES TWO AND THREE: _**Denmark cannot protect that land from Russia or China, and why do they have a "right of ownership" anyway? There are no written documents, it's only a boat that landed there hundreds of years ago, but we had boats landing there, also.**_
* It repeats the untruth that China and Russia have been threatening Denmark and ignores the fact that if they did, every NATO country including the US would be obligated to protect it. Moreover, it implies that military power ("cannot protect that land") determines legitimacy, which is a direct rejection of international law.
* It misunderstands how sovereignty works: ownership of territory is not based on who "landed a boat first," but on continuous governance, international recognition, and legal frameworks -- and ignores the fact that Greenland is actually an autonomous territory within the Kingdom of Denmark, with its own elected government and explicit self-determination rights.
* It weakens the moral and legal position of the US in opposing Russian and Chinese territorial expansion elsewhere - by mirroring Russia's justification for Ukraine and China's logic in the South China Sea: Sovereignty reduced to superpower preference and military capacity. This will almost certainly embolden these two rivals, potentially sparking wars and leading to death and destruction.
* It implies that America has a historical claim equivalent to Denmark's, which is baseless, and signals to allies that US recognition of borders is conditional and reversible.

SENTENCE FOUR: _**I have done more for NATO than any person since its founding, and now, NATO should do something for the United States.**_
* It is historically false. NATO is the product of decades of collective effort by multiple presidents, governments, militaries, and diplomats across many countries, while Trump has done much to undermine it. He has agitated against NATO for years by calling it "obsolete" and today is bringing it to the breaking point with his astounding refusal to rule out force against a NATO member.
* It ignores that NATO already "does something" for the United States every day by extending collective defense, hosting US bases, sharing intelligence, stabilizing Europe, and deterring adversaries. The only time NATO's mutual defense clause, Article V, was invoked, was for the benefit of the US after 9-11.
* It implies that NATO support is conditional on nonsense like Trump receiving personally a Nobel Peace Prize.

SENTENCE FIVE: _**The World is not secure unless we have Complete and Total Control of Greenland.**_
* It implies that global security depends on US _ownership_ of foreign territory, a claim that no serious strategic framework supports. The US cannot have total control of every territory that needs defending, or whose resources it covets.
* It again ignores that Greenland already sits inside a collective defense system that includes the United States. And the US already has extensive military access to Greenland through agreements with Denmark.
* It frames Greenland as an object to be controlled rather than a society with rights and self-determination.
* Again, the childish capitalizations - "The World," and "Complete and Total Control of Greenland." _What is up with that??_

The signoff - "Thank you! President DJT" - features his bizarre exclamation point ("Thank you for your attention to this matter!") and the sort of acronym that confers a larger-than-life status in a way no gaudy ballroom can. I suppose he wants to be thought of in the manner of an FDR or JFK (perhaps even MLK, though I actually doubt that for the obvious reason). Sadly, other acronyms entirely far more readily come to mind.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/7c52a5b4-d841-4ce8-afc8-411c3c9abdf3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Friends, honestly. It goes beyond disagreements over gun control or tax codes. There is no way this is OK. The president cannot peevishly obsess about the Nobel Prize (he actually compelled the poor actual winner, Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado,**** to "give" it to him last week in a truly twisted spectacle). And he cannot write such a letter to a foreign leader. What if he had threatened the PM's wife Marit in the style that we have grown accustomed to from the "Access Hollywood" tape? Would you _then_ agree that the shit has hit the fan? To quote Trump himself, the world is laughing at us. But it is also crying, and at the same time trembling in fear. Preparing counter-measures as well.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/11a1ec6a-18c2-4f6e-8fea-52bc1233cbad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Beyond the preposterous style and substance of the embarrassing and infantile letter, Trump's obsession with "acquiring" Greenland is a direct threat to American security. It seriously risks shattering NATO, which would cut off US access to 27 bases, risk close to $600 billion in European defense purchases, leave America without allies as its rivals are emboldened, and would precipitate a massive economic crisis. It rivals his friend Putin's invasion of Ukraine as the bonehead move of the century so far (and that bar is high).
Last month AQL awarded Trump our "[Person or Thing of the Year" award for 2025](https://substack.com/redirect/b6a5d6e1-23b7-4e4b-bf02-04e172e8a6db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which we felt was merited on account of his unequalled and impactful array of achievements. These included normalizing constitutional defiance, eroding the rule of law, and turning illegality into standard governance. It included killing untold thousands as well as US soft power by kneecapping USAID, and risking millions of others by weakening FEMA (on top of wanting to dismantle the Department of Education). He dismantled institutional checks, mainstreamed corruption by fusing personal business with state power and converting public office into a revenue stream, and empowered billionaire patrons to shape regulation for private gain. He weakened public health by promoting anti-vaccine ideology, attacked the press to suppress accountability, destabilized the economy through reckless and illegal tariffs which are a tax on Americans and not foreigners, and fractured US alliances. Since these outcomes, which many might consider negative, were willfull, they count as achievements.
But they are terrible, of course, for America and the world.
Now, I know that the Republicans who are in a position to keep Trump in check are very busy indeed, spending their days and nights licking his boots and trembling in fear of being primaried. They may not have time to consult the Constitution. So as a public service, on the cusp of one year since Trump reentered the Oval Office, I offer a handy cheat sheet.
Ratified in 1967, the Twenty-Fifth Amendment provides a constitutional mechanism for dealing with presidential incapacity. Its most consequential provision, Section 4, allows the vice president and a majority of the Cabinet to declare that the president is unable to discharge the powers and duties of the office. Upon that declaration, the vice president immediately becomes acting president. If the president contests the decision, Congress must decide the matter, and a two-thirds vote in both the House and the Senate is required to keep the president sidelined. That would mean about 20 Republican invertebrates would need to grow a spine.
This is far from likely, even after the November midterm elections, when the lemmings in Congress may feel a bit more free. Hell, the chances are actually tiny, no matter what stupidity Trump does next. But stranger things have happened. These are not many, but they do include the repeat election of "President DJT."

# NYT fumes over savage AWFUL acronym for liberal white women
The New York Times decried the rising use of "AWFUL"--**[Affluent White Female Urban Liberal](https://substack.com/redirect/8b22a5b8-aa93-4752-b67e-bcf905ca5fca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** --as a derogatory acronym among conservatives mocking liberal women protesting ICE after activist Renee Good's fatal shooting by an agent in Minneapolis on January 7.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8b22a5b8-aa93-4752-b67e-bcf905ca5fca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **AWFUL gains traction online**
Conservative commentators like Erick Erickson popularized "AWFUL" after Good's death, claiming she rammed her car into an ICE agent who fired in self-defense amid rising progressive violence.
* **NYT queries DHS on trend**
The Times contacted Homeland Security for comment on the acronym's popularity, receiving a dismissive response prioritizing "facts on the ground" over online slang amid anti-ICE unrest.
* **Tied to broader cultural clash**
The term reflects conservative backlash against affluent liberal white women, linked to voting shifts (Harris won them by 17 points in 2024) and NYT critiques framing ICE as aggressive "secret police."

# **Supreme court weighs property rights vs. gun rights in Hawaii case**
The Supreme Court's conservative majority questioned Tuesday whether Hawaii can require explicit property owner permission before[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/00dfbf15-9336-4c1d-b61b-1f5a478e6359?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[lawful gun carriers](https://substack.com/redirect/00dfbf15-9336-4c1d-b61b-1f5a478e6359?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/00dfbf15-9336-4c1d-b61b-1f5a478e6359?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)bring firearms into private businesses, examining whether property rights or Second Amendment protections should prevail.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/00dfbf15-9336-4c1d-b61b-1f5a478e6359?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **" Vampire rules" challenged:** Maui gun owners are contesting Hawaii's statute--shared by California, Maryland, New Jersey, and New York--mandating concealed-carry license holders get express approval verbally or through signage before entering public-facing private spaces like malls, stores, and gas stations, calling the default prohibition "vampire rules" since weapons cannot enter without invitation, with violations carrying up to one year imprisonment.
* **Bench sharply divided:** Justice Samuel Alito accused Hawaii of "relegating the Second Amendment to second-class status," while Justice Sonia Sotomayor countered "Is there a constitutional right to enter private property with a gun without an owner's express or implicit consent? The answer has to be simply no," as Chief Justice Josh Roberts questioned why First Amendment door-knocking rights differ from Second Amendment protections for armed political candidates.
* **Historical context emphasized:** Hawaii officials defended restrictions citing the Aloha State's tradition of limiting dangerous weapons dating to its monarchy era, with fewer than 1% of residents holding concealed-carry permits (about 2,200 licenses since the landmark 2022 Supreme Court ruling expanding gun rights outside homes), while the Trump administration supports gun owners arguing the law creates discriminatory treatment.
* * *
# **Trump marks one-year anniversary at press briefing**
President Trump made a rare White House press briefing appearance Tuesday on the one-year anniversary of his **[second term's inauguration](https://substack.com/redirect/428c705f-22e5-41af-804c-1cf9f8cf3229?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**, showcasing accomplishments while focusing heavily on criminal arrests in Minnesota.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/969aaddd-f833-4a1b-b7f7-b725fab19b5e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **Achievements:** Trump displayed a thick packet documenting his administration's work, declaring "I could stand here and read it for a week, and we wouldn't be finished" while claiming to have done "more than any other administration has done by far."
* **Minnesota-focus:** The president held up suspect photos from Minnesota immigration enforcement operations, calling them "rough characters...criminal illegal aliens...in many cases murderers...drug lords, drug dealers," emphasizing "the crime is incredible, the financial crimes are incredible" in the state amid ongoing federal crackdowns.
* **Rare briefing room visit:** Trump's appearance marked his first White House press briefing since June 27, 2025, with Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt teasing beforehand that "We've never had a president fight harder to deliver on the promises he made" while hinting at "a very special guest" joining her at the podium.

subject: There is an open conflict inside the Democratic Party
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Abdul for U
body:
[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/30?refcode=&t=1001&akid=1582%2E251025%2EnaaldM ]Abdul for US Senate [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/30?refcode=&t=1002&akid=1582%2E251025%2EnaaldM ]Abdul for US Senate

Lately, it feels like the weight of the world is on our shoulders.

Donald Trump and his goons are wreaking havoc in our communities, turning
our economy upside down, and making life worse for us — all while sending
billions of our tax dollars overseas to fuel genocide.

And I know I’m not alone in feeling this frustration.

So the question is simple,
Peter: What
are we going to do about it?

One thing that would make a tangible difference is winning back the Senate
and using our majority to stop awful MAGA bills like this from seeing the
light of day. 👇

[ Aipac ]Aipac tracker

But first, we have to decide, together, what kind of Democratic Party
we’re going to be if we want to win back the trust of voters — and
unfortunately, we’re not there yet.

There is no issue where the Democratic Party’s internal crisis is more
visible than Gaza.

Across this country — among Democrats, independents, young voters — people
are horrified that our tax dollars are being used to enable the bombing,
starvation, and genocide of children and families of Gaza.

Yet too many establishment leaders are still pretending nothing has
changed. The silence is LOUD. And some candidates are falling in line with
this strategy. Here’s what that looks like in our primary:

1. One candidate is openly embraced by AIPAC and other pro-Israel groups
like DMFI. They’ve taken the money. They’ve voted to send billions
more overseas. And they refuse to even acknowledge the reality
unfolding in Gaza.
2. Another candidate has treated this entire issue like an inconvenience
— attending closed-door AIPAC events, praising the Israel Defense
Forces, dismissing the outrage as a “political purity test,” and only
very recently, and very reluctantly, recognizing what the rest of the
world already knows.

These approaches don’t inspire anyone, and they certainly won’t move
people to believe in or fight for our vision.

Meanwhile, the establishment and groups like AIPAC are doing their best to
squash the next generation of qualified Democratic candidates (myself
included) on the basis that they are not “pro-Israel” enough.

If we’re going to withstand that pressure and win, we need to stick
together and send an unmistakable message about where the Democratic Party
needs to go. If you’re able, donating even a small amount helps us do
that:

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260120-1-ak.PrmiFf&refcode=em20260120-1580&t=1004&akid=1582%2E251025%2EnaaldM ]https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-ms-aes-20260120-1-ak?refcode=em20260120-1580

Peter, I’ve
been clear from day one: No more taxpayer dollars for genocide.

And because I’ve taken that stand — because I refuse AIPAC money and
corporate PAC money — this race has become something bigger than just
Michigan.

There is an open conflict inside the Democratic Party. Between those who
believe our path forward runs through moral clarity and people-powered
movements, and those who believe the safest route is staying quiet and
keeping donors comfortable.

That conflict is going to be decided in races like ours,
Peter.

And now that it’s officially the election year, the stakes just got real.

The money raised right now determines who builds the strongest organizing
operation, who gets the most ads on the air, and who defines the narrative
before Michigan is flooded with outside spending.

That’s why your support matters so much.

When we post strong grassroots fundraising numbers early in the year, it
sends a clear signal — to the media, to party leadership, to AIPAC and
every other special interest watching closely — that this campaign is not
fringe, not symbolic, and not going away.

If you’re able, I’m asking you to chip in today to help us start this
election year strong:

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260120-1-ak.PrmiFf&refcode=em20260120-1580&t=1005&akid=1582%2E251025%2EnaaldM ]https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-ms-aes-20260120-1-ak?refcode=em20260120-1580

Every contribution helps us build early, organize everywhere, and show
that this movement is bigger than any AIPAC check.

Thank you for taking the time to read this.

In solidarity,

Abdul

Meanwhile, the establishment and groups like AIPAC are doing their best to squash the next generation of qualified Democratic candidates (myself included) on the basis that they are not “pro-Israel” enough. If we’re going to withstand that pressure and win, we need to stick together and send an unmistakable message about where the Democratic Party needs to go. If you’re able, donating even a small amount helps us do that: [ ] Peter, I’ve been clear from day one: No more taxpayer dollars for genocide. And because I’ve taken that stand — because I refuse AIPAC money and corporate PAC money — this race has become something bigger than just Michigan. There is an open conflict inside the Democratic Party. Between those who believe our path forward runs through moral clarity and people-powered movements, and those who believe the safest route is staying quiet and keeping donors comfortable. That conflict is going to be decided in races like ours, Peter. And now that it’s officially the election year, the stakes just got real. The money raised right now determines who builds the strongest organizing operation, who gets the most ads on the air, and who defines the narrative before Michigan is flooded with outside spending. That’s why your support matters so much. When we post strong grassroots fundraising numbers early in the year, it sends a clear signal — to the media, to party leadership, to AIPAC and every other special interest watching closely — that this campaign is not fringe, not symbolic, and not going away. If you’re able, I’m asking you to chip in today to help us start this election year strong: [ ] Every contribution helps us build early, organize everywhere, and show that this movement is bigger than any AIPAC check. Thank you for taking the time to read this. In solidarity, Abdul

Dear Friend of Truth,

Imagine waking up to this message from your high school:

"Vandalism to school property. Law enforcement has been contacted and we are cooperating with the investigation."

And now, imagine that message was aimed at YOU--because you got permission to paint your school's "spirit rock" with a message commemorating Charlie Kirk and the legacy he left to Christian youth.

[ GIVE NOW](http://links.redconservatives.com/s/c/1wwJsmunw13lDeVcNby4Mcru6BLZqjwgveMKbOSnnHtSxidFcvosGHZJisnJoybmhLIZVL5Ba4Tm3QjL1uJqa9xCJC0-LwDwWi_kuCl4u9NLBWEXbsRrFvoo3G1aAU1EczNRYC_4P65ZrLT8mG-fukbPi20l0Uh-81cbe9j5QejKKaQvNgdCEJGz_q6xgxaZBuUgHUqc5ZAEeNCYobLxyXCxDjOk3589W1gdtD7q_hgJ3JHGOYWubO2IyFOOdl7RsoiIPuYoXJMyGxz-DEhCT0YFPaYcgpIKTB_9ortmFFsmpJk1Oo3ZjGvcytdr32WUW8RovG9PX787ZYp1TAhabCaaF53bieWXRB_XBYxzFcpAdRSicrIWGNNQz2NSTlI5jICRg7P6LVueG8MyEqSOIQb6OdnCIpi4uvNvHcJemrjYf3PiwpdfnyL_-AD-kQwPItTH-50eyYEqIR4BrUP4QBhRBzC4xZg9rALLMq6x0FrQvhOcdqUINAgP4LQhSpb1spOXxXlsGfF1c7zJt2YI8T9M2uSYr-53XRvWVrv4fbWsv6-8OlC4QUBzdw4N37DOxQNbOLvXGnCZH-KDSjTjfpZOEDyaUYMdWnrmLAab9CB6GhzYkxEb0Jxe5sJbpLZN3M-GIni4vkx5ejsxRc0tC88wiouvq-K3bOOeSaEf_DQ13qlXmoGw43UPpLALZcjPYuWey3-0eu9KUfZ0VgpfhXA77SFqEPnr4A/GarcOmlxCaq_X8DWTdo16Hb4vKhSBfKQ/17)

That's exactly what happened to Gabby Stout. She had expressly asked permission to paint the message--and the school had given it.

**But the next day, after she and her friends painted the rock with the messages "Freedom 1776" and "Live Like Kirk--John 11:25," school officials sent out a school-wide email accusing them of vandalism and launched a criminal investigation.**

And it got worse. The local news widely reported on the "vandalism" and "investigation"--and school officials hauled Gabby into an office and forced her to write a statement describing her actions and show them her phone logs.

School officials never obtained permission from her parents to go through her phone, nor did they inform her or her parents of her constitutional right to remain silent and contact an attorney during a criminal investigation.

Fellow Conservative

James Carville went on Fox News and declared Republicans are headed for a “wipeout” in the 2026 midterms.

[](http://links.freedomfirstalert.com/u/click?_t=9ca143e971904d26a973d002cb0ae7f7&_m=f5d855501d354b00a31572b50c55a0b8&_e=fXZI9lXIci0thRIxUG3RZUljaX2UoeExkOj4VcteprZIZcXDTdxaqAMjq8ilO0IjIKps2i1WwzDKDZU2AeB-iaJaxI6lgL8v_7G9uSfc3yiIrtHv7FlKNuCuh7YHFvSKcweZfPDZO1GwiOtC8W6QHZwK8YxuboXtLovE4kjb0u_1WPs4JzzG0WKAMuzj3YWsPAg89uXgHF3Je4iEQtuWkoC6DIysImlz6aWVSiEzjpv29yTgWuCvw_Dm6ylJJHf5IUjEUyOMtFNaM4rtSZwdKSmJwr7iBQa-GGXFYGbYUwXzk1xEhofMIjk2izNJSmYyzvdpaBcKkBhGVIoGyhxd7oymR7jaZbdiQgscydwtiw_-htUmiYM2pN5cnEXIKhZ0x12CTDg1nJm8ul9ErM_uGkSQpjKNTl1J4v5w32bdROwXCeVKfRaT6Nf6PNCAI7SBKwmZ9q3ytbQZIsym_EztADn69fdooPxwo-omHQDNkUMi_CDo-ZUxtrpl0xe2FMRrCz5gtQzOn6FTHxWYYXio5NOLj7XArtyYlX3aeUnreXpAYlHC46lt72EJuxhrvkPjjX667rmEYTE0DNHS_jZ6Px9Hf5YnuNGF2EgTnf4axehsxnHE81v7zz_F7Pr5AnKG-y4lIyItGT0zH_DfHpWlDIGdlAT8z7DV6_9sT0aC10E%3D)

**Not a setback. Not a bad night._A wipeout._**
And I’m going to be honest with you. He’s saying it out loud because Democrats can feel the wind shifting. They see early numbers. They see the money starting to move. They see the media warming up the attack machine. And they think Republicans are about to do what we’ve done too many times before: get comfortable, get distracted, and get caught flat-footed.

That is exactly what 2026 is: **a dogfight.** A fight where our Senate majority is on the line, and we’re already being treated like we’re on defense.

Democrats are laser-focused on the U.S. Senate because they know the truth. If they take it back, they can bring President Trump’s agenda to a dead stop. Border security gets blocked. Spending cuts get buried. Conservative judges get stalled. Oversight turns into vengeance. **Every ounce of momentum we earned gets smothered by Chuck Schumer and the radical Left.**

Carville is predicting a “wipeout” because Democrats want to create a self-fulfilling prophecy. They want Republicans to believe the media hype, accept defeat early, and stop fighting. They want to demoralize our voters so they can quietly claw back power seat by seat while the base is looking the other way.

But the stakes here are even bigger than one election cycle.

If Democrats get control of the Senate, they will do everything they can to sabotage President Trump and cripple his presidency. They will block his nominees, derail his reforms, and they will turn the Senate into an obstruction factory.

clean_body: | Fellow Conservative James Carville went on Fox News and declared Republicans are headed for a “wipeout” in the 2026 midterms. Not a setback. Not a bad night.A wipeout. And I’m going to be honest with you. He’s saying it out loud because Democrats can feel the wind shifting. They see early numbers. They see the money starting to move. They see the media warming up the attack machine. And they think Republicans are about to do what we’ve done too many times before: get comfortable, get distracted, and get caught flat-footed. That is exactly what 2026 is: a dogfight. A fight where our Senate majority is on the line, and we’re already being treated like we’re on defense. Democrats are laser-focused on the U.S. Senate because they know the truth. If they take it back, they can bring President Trump’s agenda to a dead stop. Border security gets blocked. Spending cuts get buried. Conservative judges get stalled. Oversight turns into vengeance. Every ounce of momentum we earned gets smothered by Chuck Schumer and the radical Left. Carville is predicting a “wipeout” because Democrats want to create a self-fulfilling prophecy. They want Republicans to believe the media hype, accept defeat early, and stop fighting. They want to demoralize our voters so they can quietly claw back power seat by seat while the base is looking the other way. But the stakes here are even bigger than one election cycle. If Democrats get control of the Senate, they will do everything they can to sabotage President Trump and cripple his presidency. They will block his nominees, derail his reforms, and they will turn the Senate into an obstruction factory. And yes, they will impeach him again. You know it. I know it. body:
As a former Navy SEAL, I thrive in tough fights. I’ve faced worse odds overseas and am ready to bring that same grit to Washington |

---

Fellow Conservative,

My name is Adam Schwarze, and I’m a former Navy SEAL, Marine Corps veteran, and proud Minnesotan **running for U.S. Senate against Tim Walz’s handpicked lieutenant governor—a politician even more radical than her boss.** I’m requesting your support in this critical battle to restore common-sense conservative values to Minnesota.

I hold a Master’s from Harvard, a Master’s Certificate from Johns Hopkins in Security and Nuclear Deterrence, and an MBA. clean_body: As a former Navy SEAL, I thrive in tough fights. I’ve faced worse odds overseas and am ready to bring that same grit to Washington | Fellow Conservative, My name is Adam Schwarze, and I’m a former Navy SEAL, Marine Corps veteran, and proud Minnesotan running for U.S. Senate against Tim Walz’s handpicked lieutenant governor—a politician even more radical than her boss. I’m requesting your support in this critical battle to restore common-sense conservative values to Minnesota. I hold a Master’s from Harvard, a Master’s Certificate from Johns Hopkins in Security and Nuclear Deterrence, and an MBA. But my proudest achievement is serving our country to make my parents, especially my mom, proud. I want to serve you in the U.S. Senate, fighting for the values that have made Minnesota and America great for generations. I’m starting this race with absolutely nothing , but because of the enormity of the race's outcome, I figured there is no harm in asking for your help. At the end of the day, my request of you will end in one of two ways: 1.) . 2.) you read this email without contributing, but you at least now know who I am. I’m not a career politician. I’m a regular guy from a working-class family who grew up playing hockey and answered our nation’s call on my 18th birthday in October 2001, just weeks after the 9/11 attacks. I joined the Marine Corps to defend our country, and as a Navy SEAL, I deployed nine times to over 70 countries, risking my life to protect our freedoms and way of life. Unlike Tim Walz, who retired from the National Guard before his unit deployed to Iraq, I never backed down from serving our nation during war. Minnesota is at a crossroads. Under Governor Walz and his lieutenant governor, our state has been dragged left by radical policies that fueled the violent unrest in Minneapolis in 2020, defunded our police , and burdened hardworking families with higher taxes and inflation. While our streets burned, the lieutenant governor pushed lawsuits against law enforcement, undermining the officers keeping us safe. This isn’t the Minnesota I grew up in—or the one any Minnesotan deserves. If you are reading this email right now and you don’t live in Minnesota, then I’m sure you’ll agree with me that every American must be represented by individuals in Congress who want to build a better version of the America we live in today—individuals of integrity. That’s not who my opponent is. We have an incredible opportunity to elect a Republican to the U.S. Senate next year - something voters in this state haven’t done since they re-elected former Senator Norm Coleman in 2002. As a Republican, I know the odds are tough in a state that hasn’t voted red in a presidential election since 1976. But as a former Navy SEAL, I thrive in tough fights. I’ve faced worse odds overseas and am ready to bring that same grit to Washington. Here’s what I stand for: Restoring law and order by supporting our police and cracking down on crime. Cutting taxes and regulations to ease the burden on retirees and small businesses. Securing our borders to protect our communities and sovereignty. Defending our Second Amendment rights and traditional values. Stopping the radical left’s agenda that’s eroding the America we love. You don’t know me, but you know what men like me stand for and our reputation. So, . This race won’t be easy. The Democrats have deep pockets, and the radical left will stop at nothing to keep this seat. I’m running to serve you, to protect our way of life, and to ensure Minnesota remains a place where faith, family, and freedom thrive. I hope you’ll invest in me right now – any amount will help. With gratitude, Adam Schwarze Republican Candidate for U.S. Senate - Minnesota FOLLOW ADAM ON SOCIAL MEDIA** | | Paid for by Schwarze for Senate
